Hoc ergo probandum tibi restat sacrarum literarum testimonijs, Deum alicubi mandasse, vt, quos ipse videtur nobis propter cômissum aliquod facinus odisse, à conuenticulo Presbyterorum ad hoc delectorum, (causa tamen prius, vt in iudicijs fieri solet, auditis prius testibus, disceptata) solenniter declarentur à Deo in coelis exclusi è coelesti regno. Vides quid sit absq; sacris literis loqui?
units.tr: Sixthly, as though it were granted by everyone, you boldly assume that God has somewhere commanded (though you do not say where) that those contaminated by some crime should be solemnly proclaimed, by a ritual pronouncement of a council of Presbyters, to be excommunicated, with the sentence having been passed by God in heaven. Each person should be declared shut out by God in the way the holy letters teach. Others do this, but above all the ministers, when publicly and privately they set before everyone, one by one, the wrath and judgment of God against sins, and explain what punishment awaits any wicked persons (unless they return to the right way and are reconciled to God). What remains, then, is for you to prove from the testimonies of the holy letters that God has commanded somewhere that those whom he himself seems to hate on account of some committed crime should be solemnly declared by God to be shut out of the heavenly kingdom by a gathering of Presbyters chosen for this purpose. The cause, however, must first be debated, as is customary in judicial proceedings, after witnesses have been heard. Do you see what it is to speak without the holy letters?

units.la: Septimò fallis teipsum tua illa definitione, cum putas eũ, qui vel à Ministro, vel ab alio quopiam, vel à consessu Presbyterorũ pronunciatus sit à Deo in coelis condemnatus, nisi resipiscat, mox etiã in terris arceri à Sacramētis posse. Quo scripturæ testimonio probabis. (Hanc enim solã in hac re & causa audire parati sumus) Sacramenta hic in terris neganda illis esse, quos Deus videtur suo regno indignos iudicare, dummodò eis rectè (de externo ritu loquor. Cor enim soli Deo notum est) nobiscum uti desiderent? Permultos non probauit Christus, plurimis etiam iram. Dei denunciarunt & declararunt Apostoli, quorum tamen nullum à Sacramentis abstinere iusserunt. An non quotidie ministri in publicis concionibus & priuatis exhortationibus testificantur multis, non fore eos caelestis regni haeredes, nisi resipiscant, moresque cum vita mutent, quos tamen neque ipsi neq; alij à sacramentis repellunt? At non faciunt publicè, inquies & cum authoritate. Nugæ sunt. Quoniã scriptura nullo in loco tradit, maius esse, (quod ad Deum attinet) si quis à pluribus declaretur malus, quàm si ab vno solo talis demonstretur. Si vnum illum non habere hanc authoritatem obijcias, quæram ego vicissim ex te, quis pluribus istis Presbyteris eam donauerit?
units.tr: Seventhly, you deceive yourself with that definition of yours, when you think that one who has been pronounced condemned by God in heaven, unless he repents, by a minister, or by someone else, or by an assembly of Presbyters, can at once also be kept from the sacraments on earth. By what testimony of Scripture will you prove this? (For in this matter and cause we are ready to hear only this.) That the sacraments here on earth must be denied to those whom God seems to judge unworthy of his kingdom, provided they desire to use them with us rightly? (I speak of the outward rite, for the heart is known to God alone.) Christ did not approve of many, and the Apostles declared and proclaimed the wrath of God to many, yet they ordered none of them to abstain from the sacraments. Do not ministers every day, in public sermons and private exhortations, testify to many that they will not be heirs of the heavenly kingdom unless they repent and change their manners and their life; yet neither they nor others repel these same people from the sacraments? But, you will say, they do not do this publicly and with authority. These are trifles! For Scripture nowhere teaches that it is worse, so far as God is concerned, for someone to be declared wicked by many than to be shown to be such by one alone. If you object that the one man lacks this authority, I will ask you in turn: who gave that authority to those many Presbyters?

units.la: Octauò non minus falleris, cum declarationem iudicij in caelis facti idem esse putas cum excommunicatione. An idé sunt, declarare aliquē à Deo propter peccatū aliquod odio haberi, & ex visibili Ecclesia expulsum esse? Si idé sunt, tunc cuicunq; à ministris hoc siue in publico, siue in priuato loco prædicatur, is mox pro excōmunicato erit habendus. Vndè nāq; probabitur publicā declaratione Presbyterorū hoc habere, priuatā vnius vel ministri vel alterius cuiuslibet nō habere? Quod ex verbo Dei recte iudicatur, id æquè firmū validūq; est, siue ab vno solo iudicetur & pronūciétur, siue à pluribus. Nam neque à multitudine iudicantium aliquid acquirit veritas, neque à paucitate aliquid amittit. Denique tam est inutilis hæc ratiocinatio, Deus hunc hominem non iudicat dignum coelesti regno, Ergo est ex visibili Ecclesia pellendus, quàm viciosa hæc est, Deus hunc non dignabitur vita æterna, Ergò neque caduca & mortali vita eum vult viuere. Sanè Hypocritas æterna vita non donabit: quos tamè nullus ideò putet hac vita priuandos esse. An ignoramus Deum multis, quos participare coelestem vitam non patietur, facultatem nihilominus concessisse dæmonia in suo nomine expellendi, aliáq; miracula faciendi? Math. 7.
units.tr: Eighthly, you are no less mistaken when you think that a declaration of judgment made in heaven is the same thing as excommunication. Are they the same: to declare that someone is hated by God on account of some sin, and to have him expelled from the visible Church? If they are the same, then whoever is proclaimed in this way by ministers, whether in a public or a private place, must at once be held as excommunicated. For how will it be proved that a public declaration by the Presbyters has this force, while a private declaration by one minister, or by anyone else, does not? What is rightly judged from the Word of God is equally firm and valid whether it is judged and pronounced by one alone or by many. For truth gains nothing from the multitude of those who judge it, nor loses anything from their small number. Finally, this reasoning is as useless as it is faulty: "God does not judge this man worthy of the heavenly kingdom; therefore he must be expelled from the visible Church." It is just as faulty as this: "God will not count him worthy of eternal life; therefore he does not want him to live even this frail and mortal life." Certainly God will not grant eternal life to hypocrites, yet no one would therefore think they must be deprived of this life. Do we not know that God has nonetheless granted to many, whom he will not allow to share the heavenly life, the power of casting out demons in his name and of working other miracles? Math. 7.

units.la: 9 Scribis etiam te multis de causis non probare, quòd solam Sacramentorum exclusionem vrgeam: cùm vix duas adferas, easq; admodùm lubricas. Vnà est, quod excommunicationis pars præcipua sit seclusio ab interiore Christi societate: quam perspicuè ostendi huc non pertinere, inque nullius hominis potestate esse. Altera est, posse aliquem ad cœnæ participationem non admitti, vt tamen non excommunicetur: quæ opus habet consideratione. Si enim de pueris, & in doctrina nondum institutis, ac mysterium hoc non intelligentibus loqueris, libenter assentior. Si autem de illis intelligis (vt intelligere te oportet, si de proposita causa agis) qui propter obscœnitatem antea&æ vitæ remouentur à cœnæ vsurpatione, tibi ipsi contradicis. Tu enim hanc rem gradum excommunicationis fecisti, cum sic scribis. Et varij quoq; sunt Excommunicationis gradus pro varijs non tantùm peccatorum inter se, sed etiam vnius & eiusdem peccati circumstantijs: quò fit, vt nonnulli hactenus tantùm ex communi coetu eijciantur, quatenùs eis ad tempus interdicitur cœnæ participatione. Haec à te cum ibi dicta sint, cur hic mutes, non video: nisi fortè istud vidisti pugnarecum tua definitione. Quippè conscia Ecclesia excommunicationem fieri, habet definitio: cum ista prohibitio quotidiè possit fieri in solo Presbyterorum consessu. At constat, nullum esse inter hanc & alteram excommunicationè discrimen, quàm quod haec priuata quodammodo, illa publica est. De Sacramentorum negatione præcipuè ob id disputo, quia vt à me probatum est, Excommunicationis vis in ea principaliter consistit: vt quia in omnem difciplinam Ecclesiæ facilè consensurus sum, cui non admisseatur cœnæ Dominicæ prohibitio. Non enim in hunc finem à Domino instituta est: sed vt sit læta gratiarum actio, publica mortis Christi prædicatio, pietatis & fidei exercitium, mutuæque dilectionis vinculum. Scelerum coercendorum aliam rationem præscripsit Ecclesiæ suæ Dominus: qua neglecta non decet nos, quam finxerunt sibi homines, arripere, & mordicus cum Ecclesiæ pernicie defendere. A tua sententia non discedunt alij, qui excommunicationem contendunt eiectione è Regno Dei, (cuius testimonium duntaxat sit negatio Sacramentorum) definiendam. Quippe partem esse dicunt ministerij: quod interiorem hominem per se non attingit. Nam minister externus rigat & plantat externè: incrementum autem intus dat solus Deus. Deinde fatentur ijdem vnà tecum & cum scholasticis, nullum rite excommunicari, qui non sit à Deo prius exclusus. Itaque per Regnum Dei non possunt aliud, quàm externum, seu Ecclesiam visibilem intelligere. Quòd si ita est, & neque possent neque debent vlli homines ab auditione, seu lectione, neque diuini verbi: à precibus, & invocatione publica nominis Dei: denique à veritatis consessione arceri: superest vt duntaxat à Sacramentorum participatione amoueantur. Quippe quibus iam dictorum nihil deest, pro seclusis ab externo Ecclesiæ cœtu non habentur. Quibus autem aliquid horum deest, illi iam ab omnibus pro abiunctis reputantur: etiamsi solenniter eos nemo damnauerit. Quæ præter hæc sunt, accidentia sunt excommunicationis: non sunt essentiæ partes. Etenim, testibus sacris literis, insunt, ac non insunt (aut saltem insse ac non insse possunt plurimis) siue ad Sacramenta admittantur, siue non admittantur. Cæterùm quod ab interna & spirituali coniunctione Christi & Ecclesiæ nullus homo nos possit separare: quódquæ quódque à solaexterna societate fidelium excludat excommunicatio, probaui hoc argumento in Thesibus. Is tantùm Christo nos coniungere, autàb eius societate spirituali auellere abripereq; potest, qui veram in nobis fidem gignere, genitamq; iterum exstinguere potest. Quippè per solam fidem Christo inserimur, viuaq; eius membra efficimur: & è contrà, propter solam infidelitatem membra Christi esse desiniemus. At veram in nobis fiduciam accendere, accensamque exstinguere nulli possunt homines nullæque creaturæ. Proinde nulli nos possunt homines ab interna Christi societate separare. His tu præteritis, respondere conaris ad alia quædam in primo scripto, (quod mihi ad memoriam ab initio tumultuariè, vt quouis tempore quodlibet occurrebat, conscripseram, & in quod rudem & impolitam adhuc materiam velut in aceruum conieceram, vt ocium naƈtus aptè disponerem) contenta: sed non maiore felicitate earesellisti, quàm supra definitionem labefaƈtare studuisti.
units.tr: 9 You also write that for many reasons you do not approve of my urging exclusion from the sacraments alone, since you bring forward hardly two reasons, and those very slippery ones. The first is that the principal part of excommunication is seclusion from the inner fellowship of Christ, which I have clearly shown does not belong here and is in no man's power. The second is that someone may be refused admission to the Supper and yet not be excommunicated; this point deserves consideration. If you are speaking of children, and of those not yet instructed in doctrine, who do not understand this mystery, I readily agree. But if you mean those who (as you must mean if you are dealing with the cause proposed) are kept from the use of the Supper on account of the foulness of their earlier life, then you contradict yourself. For you have made this matter a degree of excommunication when you write: "There are also various degrees of excommunication, according to the various circumstances not only of different sins but also of one and the same sin; whence it comes that some, hitherto, are only cast out of the common assembly, insofar as for a time they are forbidden participation in the Supper." Since you said this there, I do not see why you change it here, unless perhaps you saw that it conflicted with your definition. For your definition holds that excommunication is an act of the knowing Church, whereas this prohibition could be made every day in the sole assembly of the Presbyters. Yet it is established that there is no difference between this and the other excommunication, except that this one is in a way private and that one public. I argue about the denial of the sacraments especially for this reason: as I have proved, the force of excommunication consists chiefly in it. And I shall readily agree to admit prohibition from the Lord's Supper into every discipline of the Church. For the Lord did not institute the Supper for this end, but so that it might be a joyful thanksgiving, a public proclamation of the death of Christ, an exercise of piety and faith, and a bond of mutual love. The Lord prescribed for his Church another method of restraining sins. If that is neglected, it is not fitting for us to seize what men have devised for themselves and to defend it stubbornly to the ruin of the Church. Others who contend that excommunication should be defined as ejection from the Kingdom of God (of which the sole testimony is the denial of the sacraments) do not depart from your opinion. For they say that it is a part of the ministry, which does not touch the inner man by itself: the external minister waters and plants outwardly, but God alone gives the increase within. Next, these same men agree with you and with the schoolmen that no one is rightly excommunicated who has not first been excluded by God. So by the Kingdom of God they can understand nothing other than the external or visible Church. But if this is so, and no men can or ought to be kept from hearing or reading the divine word, from prayers and the public invocation of the name of God, and finally from confessing the truth, what remains is that they be removed only from participation in the sacraments. For those who lack none of the things just mentioned are not regarded as cut off from the external assembly of the Church. But those who lack any of these are already reckoned by everyone as separated, even if no one has solemnly condemned them. Whatever lies beyond these are accidents of excommunication, not parts of its essence. For, as the holy letters bear witness, they are present or absent (or at least can be present or absent in very many people) whether men are admitted to the sacraments or not. Moreover, that no man can separate us from the inner and spiritual union of Christ and the Church, and that excommunication cuts off only from the external fellowship of the faithful, I proved by this argument in the Theses. Only he can join us to Christ, or tear us away from his spiritual fellowship, who can beget true faith in us and extinguish it once begotten. For we are grafted into Christ through faith alone and become living members of him; and conversely, on account of unbelief alone we cease to be members of Christ. But no men and no creature can kindle true trust in us, or extinguish it once kindled. Therefore no men can separate us from the inner fellowship of Christ. Passing over these points, you try to reply to certain other things in my first writing, which I had hastily composed from the beginning for my own memory, as each thing occurred to me at any time, and into which I had thrown the still rough and unpolished material as into a heap, intending to arrange it properly when I had leisure. But you have been no more successful in refuting these things than you have been eager to undermine my definition.

units.la: Ad primum, quod sic habet: Salutem nobis homines neque dare, neque adimere possunt: quapropter non potuerit excommunicatio abscissione salutis definiri: ita respondes. Seruare & perdere, soluere & ligare, aperire & claudere, remittere peccata & retinere, etiam hominibus tribuuntur, vt Dei Ministris. Non enim subordinata causa repugnare potest primariæ causæ, cui serviunt. Paulò supra dixisti, excommunicare nil esse aliud, quam denunciare alicui, quod à Deo in cœlis reiectus fit, dum redeat in viam. At hæc denunciatio non est salutis abscissio. Etenim qui salutem mihi à Deo indicat negatam, is eam mihi non aufert: sed ablatam à Deo mihi tantùm significat. Certè minister magistratus sententiam alicui denuncians non fert ipse sententiam, sed latam à Magistratu nunciat. Quod si ergo salutem alicui negare, vel è societate visibilis Ecclesiæ exturbare, seu excommunicare, aliud nihil est, quàm recte diuinis literis alicui renunciare quod à Deo sit reiectus, tantisper dum vitam moresq; suos emendet, sublata è medio est omnis inter nos controuersia. Sed ex hac declaratione, inquies, consequitur, cum, qui in coelis iudicatus sit indignus societate Christi, ne in terris quidem inter membra externae Ecclesiae Christi censendum esse. Ego vero hoc ex illo consequi pernego: & te nullo vnquam tempore probaturum esse incunctanter affirmo. Quippe vt ratiocinatio tua valeat, propositionem oportet vniuersalem esse (Nam ex solis particularibus nihil concludi potest) Proinde veram esse hanc oportet: quisquis à Deo iudicatur indignus regno coelesti, à Senioribus est eijciendus ex Ecclesiae visibilis consociatione. At manifeste salsa est. Semper enim plus palea quam frumenti: plus zizaniae quam tritici: plus denique malorum, quam bonorum in Ecclesia visibili fuerunt, sunt, erunt. Ipsemet Christus Math. 20. & 22. dicit, Multos quidem esse vocatos at paucos electos. Et alibi viam ad interitum spaciosam esse, cum, quae ad vitam ducit angusta sit admodum. Quocirca si vera esset propositio, semper oporteret longè plures esse excommunicatos quam incommunicatos: quod est absurdum cogitatu.
units.tr: As for the first point, which runs: "Men can neither give us salvation nor take it away, so excommunication cannot be defined as the removal of salvation." You answer that to save and to destroy, to loose and to bind, to open and to shut, to remit sins and to retain them, are also attributed to men as ministers of God. A subordinate cause cannot oppose the primary cause it serves. A little earlier you said that to excommunicate is nothing other than to declare to someone that he has been cast off by God in heaven, for as long as he does not return to the right way. But this declaration is not a removal of salvation. For whoever tells me that salvation has been denied me by God does not take it away; he only signifies that it has been taken from me by God. Certainly a minister of the magistrate who announces a sentence to someone does not pass the sentence himself; he reports the sentence passed by the magistrate. So if to deny someone salvation, or to expel him from the fellowship of the visible Church, or to excommunicate him, is nothing else than to declare to him, from the divine writings, that he has been rejected by God for as long as he does not amend his life and conduct, then all controversy between us is removed. But, you will say, it follows from this declaration that whoever has been judged unworthy of fellowship with Christ in heaven must not be counted even on earth among the members of the external Church of Christ. I flatly deny that this follows from that, and I confidently affirm that you will never prove it. For if your reasoning is to hold, the proposition must be universal (for nothing can be concluded from particular premises alone). Therefore this proposition must be true: whoever is judged by God unworthy of the heavenly kingdom must be cast out of the fellowship of the visible Church by the elders. But it is plainly false. For there has always been, is now, and will be in the visible Church more chaff than wheat, more tares than wheat, and in short more evil than good. Christ himself says in Matthew 20 and 22 that many are called but few are chosen. And elsewhere he says that the way that leads to destruction is broad, while the way that leads to life is very narrow. Therefore, if the proposition were true, there would always have to be far more excommunicated than uncommunicated people, which is absurd to think.

units.la: Quod si respondeas, parabolas illas non esse exponendas de publicè notis peccatoribus, sed de Hypocritis & occultè peccantibus, te autem loqui de illis, quorum scelera sint nota, tunc propositio sic erit formanda. Quecunque Deus notum Ecclesiae peccatorem apud se in coelis damnauerit, eundem quoque vult à Senioribus ex visibilis Ecclesiae societate eijci. At non plus est in hac, quam in illa, firmitatis. Primùm enim falsum est, adducta scripturae loca de solis occultis & ignotis loqui peccatoribus. Etenim parabola de palea & tritico: itèm de zizania seminata in agro tritici: item de invitatis ad nuptias, hanc interpretationem manifestè respuunt. Sanè in parabola de zizania Math. 13. clarè disterteque ponitur, ministros & seruos Domini cognouisse & distinxisse zizaniam à tritico. De duabus reliquis id tantùm dicam, imò veluti digito indicabo potius, quod Augustinus contrà Donatistas disputans scripsit. Cùm enim Donatistae parabolam de malis & bonis piscibus sic eluderent, ideo nō potuisse malos à bonis separari à Piscatoribus, quia sub aquis latuerint, respondet eis Augustinus: vt maximè latuerint mali pisces, at non latuit palea, nec latuit aliena veste indutus in nuptijs. De quo idem in lib. contrà Donatistas post collationem cap. 20. sic scribit. Ideò & illum, qui non habebat vestem nuptialem, non illi, qui inuitauerunt, sed ipse Dominus, cuius erat conuiuium, ligari iussit & proijci. Neque enim & ipse sicut pisces, sub fluctibus erat: & sic ab inuitatoribus, quomodò piscis à Piscatoribus, videri non poterat. Proinde ne putaretur sicut isti putant, quod velut vnus in turba latenter subrepsisset ignaris, continuò Dominus in eodem vno, quem ligatis manibus & pedibus ex illo conuiuio in tenebras exteriores proijci iussit, multam societatem malorum esse intelligendam, (inter quos pauciores boni in conuiuio Dominico viuunt) significare non dissulit. Nam postquam dixit, ligate illi manus & pedes, & proijcite eum in tenebras exteriores vbi erit fletus & stridor dentium, continuò subiecit. Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci verò electi. Qui plura cupit, legat eiusdem lib. cap. 10. de palea & zizania. Secundò falsum illud quoque est, Deum in sanctis scripturis alicubi praecepisse, vt quoscunque ipse notos Ecclesiae malos coelo indignos iudicet, nos è societate externa Ecclesiae exturbemus. Imperauit quidem Magistratui vt facinorosos excommunicet (qui si negligens in hac parte fuerit, iram Dei nõ effugiet) ac Presbyteris aut aliis quibusdam sub Christiano Magistratu degentibus hoc à Deo munus officiumque commissum esse tum credam, cum loco ex sacris literis producto mihi demonstratum fuerit.
units.tr: But if you reply that those parables are not to be explained of publicly known sinners, but of hypocrites and of those who sin in secret, and that you are speaking of those whose wickedness is known, then the proposition will have to be framed thus: whatever known sinner of the Church God has condemned in heaven, the same God also wills to be cast out by the elders from the fellowship of the visible Church. But this has no more firmness than the other. For first, it is false that the cited passages of Scripture speak only of hidden and unknown sinners. Indeed, the parable of the chaff and the wheat, likewise the parable of the tares sown in the field of wheat, and likewise that of those invited to the wedding, plainly reject this interpretation. In the parable of the tares in Matthew 13 it is clearly and distinctly stated that the ministers and servants of the Lord knew the tares and separated them from the wheat. Of the two remaining parables I will say only this, or rather I will point to them as with a finger, as Augustine wrote when disputing against the Donatists. When the Donatists evaded the parable of the good and bad fish by arguing that the bad fish could not be separated from the good by the fishermen because they had lain hidden under the waters, Augustine answers them: however well the bad fish were hidden, the chaff was not hidden, nor was the man hidden who was clothed in another's garment at the wedding. On this same point, in his book against the Donatists after the conference, chapter 20, he writes thus: "So it was that the one who did not have a wedding garment was ordered to be bound and cast out, not by those who had invited him, but by the Lord himself, whose feast it was. For he was not, like fish, under the waves, and so he could not be seen by those who invited him as a fish could not be seen by the fishermen. Therefore, lest it be thought, as those men think, that he had crept in unnoticed among the crowd of ignorant people, the Lord, in that one man whom he ordered to be cast out of that feast into the outer darkness with his hands and feet bound, did not hesitate to signify that there is to be understood a large fellowship of evil men (among whom the good who live at the Lord's feast are fewer). For after he said, 'Bind his hands and feet, and cast him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth,' he immediately added, 'For many are called, but few are chosen.'" Whoever wants more should read the same book, chapter 10, on the chaff and the tares. Secondly, it is also false that God has anywhere in the holy Scriptures commanded that whichever known evil persons of the Church he judges unworthy of heaven, we should expel from the external fellowship of the Church. He has indeed commanded the magistrate to excommunicate wicked criminals (and if he is negligent in this, he will not escape the wrath of God), and I would believe that this duty and office has been committed by God to elders, or to others living under a Christian magistrate, only when a passage from the sacred writings has been shown to me.

units.la: Ad argumentum quod attinet, breuis, clara, certa est responsio. Homines etiā soluunt, ligant, aperiunt, claudunt, salutè dant ac negant, peccata remittunt ac retinent eo modo, quē in scripturis Deus expresserit. Tuum ergo iam erit nos docere locum in sacris libris, in quo Deus mandet, vt cum aliquis foedè viuit, quidā Presbyteri conueniant, & suis sententijs hominē illū ex visibili caetu Ecclesiae expellant atq; à sacramētis abstinere cogant, dū suā eis pœnitentiā probārit.
units.tr: As to the argument, the answer is brief, clear and certain. Men also loose, bind, open, shut, give and deny salvation, and remit and retain sins, in the way that God has expressed in the Scriptures. It will therefore be your task to show us a passage in the sacred books in which God commands that when someone lives shamefully, certain elders should meet and by their sentences expel that man from the visible assembly of the Church and compel him to abstain from the sacraments until he shows them his repentance.

units.la: Hæc Hęc nisi probes, inaniter verbá fundes hac de re. Ex Dei verbo docendi sunt homines quæ sit eius erga nos voluntas, quidq; vicissim à nobis ille postulet. Qui his fide habet, soluitur: qui contemnit, ligatur. Qui salutis annuntiationem putat eiusdem esse collationem, aut irę Dei aduersus peccatum declarationem, existimat eiusdē esse executionem, nimis turpiter errat. Non enim Prophetæ, cum populum in captiuitatem abductum iri promulgarunt, ipsi eum vinctum abduxerunt. Nec minister Principis aut magistratus, cum Domini sententiam aliqua de re latam denuntiat, ipse eam tulit. Quod si ficremittant ac retineant peccata, soluuant ac ligent homines, quomodo tu vis, non erunt ipsi subordinatæ causæ Dei, sed alienæ & extra Dei ordine positæ. Ergo cum, non Conciliabulum illud Presbyterorum, sed alius quiuis ebrioso conuićto sic prędicat: Ebriosos pronuntiat Deus non habere partem in regno Dei, nisi resipiscant.
units.tr: Unless you prove this, you pour out empty words on this matter. From the word of God men must be taught what his will toward us is, and what in turn he demands from us. Whoever believes these things is loosed; whoever despises them is bound. Whoever thinks that the announcement of salvation belongs to the same person who confers it, or the declaration of God's wrath against sin belongs to the same person who executes it, errs most shamefully. For when the prophets proclaimed that the people would be led away into captivity, they did not themselves lead them away in chains. Nor, when the minister of a prince or magistrate announces a sentence that the lord has pronounced on some matter, does he himself pronounce it. But if men remit and retain sins, loose and bind, as you wish, they will not be subordinate causes of God, but foreign to him and placed outside the order of God. Therefore, when it is not that conventicle of elders but any other person who says this to a convicted drunkard, namely that God declares drunkards have no part in the kingdom of God unless they repent, he is not excommunicating him, but simply reporting what God has said.

units.la: Tu Ebriosus es. Ergo
units.tr: You are a drunkard. Therefore

units.la: Nisi resipiscas non habebis partem in regno Dei. Hoc, inquam, qui conuićto denuntiat, Dei iudicium denuntiat, fateor. At cum postea annećtis Syllogismum alterum illū, nihil aliud facis, quàm petis principium: hoc est, sumis vt probatum, quod nec probauisti, nec probare in sempiternum poteris. Syllogismus tuus hic est: Quos pronunciauit Dominus non habere partem in regno suo, quamdiu non resipiscunt, indignum est alia conditione censeri in terris in cœtu fidelium. Hunc constat talem esse, dum ad pœnitentiam reuocari non potest.
units.tr: "Unless you repent, you will not have a share in the kingdom of God." I grant that whoever announces this to a convicted drunkard announces the judgment of God. But when you then attach your other syllogism, you do nothing except beg the question: that is, you take for granted what you have not proved and never will be able to prove. Your syllogism runs thus: Those whom the Lord has declared to have no share in his kingdom, as long as they do not repent, are unworthy to be counted on earth in the assembly of the faithful. It is agreed that this holds while the man cannot be recalled to repentance.

units.la: Reijciatur ergo ex cœtu fidelium donec poenitentiam egerit.
units.tr: Let him therefore be cast out of the assembly of the faithful until he has repented.

units.la: Possem vno me hinc verbo expedire ac dicere, me de illis loqui, qui se pœnitere, & vitam emendare cupere affirmant, licet subinde vel per negligentiam, vel per incontinentiam etiam inuiti relabantur. Sed repetam nihilominus quędam. Si idem signisicant omnes hæ orationes: nempe Excommunicari: non censeri inter fideles in terris: eiçi ex visibili cœtu fidelium: negare alicui salutem: si inquam prædicta omnes orationes idem significent, quod hæc significat, denuntiare seu declarare alicui voluntatem ac iudicium Dei ex sacris literis: libenter admitto argumentum. At si hæc phrasis, non censeri inter fideles in terris, significat aliud, nempe Sacramentorum interdictionem vel solam, vel cum alijs quibusdam poenis coniunctam, cogita tu ipse, an, quæ hic adfers, digna sint responsione. Quatuor tibi hæc scripturis firmè ac solidè probanda nôris, si aliquid obtinere cupis. Primum est, Deum præcepisse, ut, quos cœlesti vita ipse non iudicat dignos, ex visibili coetu Ecclesiæ eiiciantur per sententiam à Presbyteris ad hoc delectis, velut in publico iudicio, per suffragia latam. Alterum est ad Sacramenta non esse admittendos, qui flagitio aliquo ita se contaminarunt, ut Presbyteris videantur Deum habere iratum, etiamsi dicant se poenitere, priusquam Presbyteris illis viti sint serio poenitere. Tertium est, Deum velle, ut quos ipse propter peccata odit, per Senatum Presbyterorum collecta per suffragia sententia arceantur à Sacramentis. Quartum, cuius similiter probationem abs te expectabimus (vide modo tu, ne frustra expectem) hoc est, nempe Deum in scripturis mandasse talem Senatum Presbyterorum sub pio Magistratu eligere, quorum iurisdictio alia sit à Magistratus potestate: quinq; facultatem habeant turpiter viuentes publica sententia arcendi à Sacramentis. Quantisper haec non probaueris, frustra tum definitionem tum Theses nostras confutare conaberis.
units.tr: I could dispose of this with one word and say that I am speaking of those who affirm that they repent and wish to amend their lives, even though they sometimes slip back, through carelessness or incontinence, against their will. Yet I will nonetheless go over some points. If all these phrases mean the same thing, namely "to be excommunicated", "not to be counted among the faithful on earth", "to be cast out of the visible assembly of the faithful", "to deny someone salvation", then, I say, if all the phrases mentioned mean what this one means, namely to announce or declare to someone the will and judgment of God from the sacred letters, I gladly accept the argument. But if the phrase "not to be counted among the faithful on earth" means something else, namely the interdiction of the sacraments, either alone or joined with certain other penalties, then consider for yourself whether what you bring forward deserves an answer. You must firmly and solidly prove four things from Scripture, if you wish to gain anything. The first is that God has commanded that those whom he himself does not judge worthy of the heavenly life be cast out of the visible assembly of the Church by a sentence pronounced by elders chosen for this purpose, as in a public trial, by vote. The second is that those who have so defiled themselves with some crime that the elders think God is angry with them are not to be admitted to the sacraments, even if they say they repent, unless they have seriously repented before the elders are satisfied. The third is that God wills that those whom he himself hates for their sins be kept from the sacraments by a sentence collected by vote of a senate of elders. The fourth, for which we shall likewise expect proof from you (see to it that I do not expect in vain), is that God has commanded in the Scriptures that such a senate of elders be chosen under a godly magistrate, whose jurisdiction is other than the power of the magistrate, and that they have the authority to exclude from the sacraments, by public sentence, those who live shamefully. As long as you have not proved these things, you will try in vain to refute both our definition and our theses.

units.la: Argumentum secundum hoc fuit. (Sic enim recito, ut à te posita sint.) Si excommunicatio definienda esset abscissione salutis, omnes excommunicati perderentur. At multi horum seruati sunt: multi etiam ex illis, qui restituti fuerunt ab excommunicatoribus, non sunt seruati. Respondes rectè, id tantum esse ratum coram Deo, quod Presbyterium rité ex verbo Dei decernit. Huic responsioni tuæ assumptionem hanc addo: At nihil tale rité ex verbo
units.tr: The second argument was this. (I recite it thus, as you set it down.) If excommunication were to be defined as the cutting off of salvation, all the excommunicated would perish. But many of them have been saved; and many of those who were restored by their excommunicators have not been saved. You rightly reply that only that is valid before God which the eldership rightly decrees from the Word of God. To this reply of yours I add this assumption: But nothing of that kind is rightly done from the Word

units.la: Dei geritur à Presbyterio. Quid sequatur, non ignoras. Quis suit vnquam excommunicator, (siue Episcopus, siue Presbiter fuerit) qui voluerit videri iniuste egisse? Et quis, quaeso te, de iniuria conqueratur? An non statim contumax talis reputaretur, & contemptor ordinis Diuini à censoribus istis censeretur? Sed, vt dixi, responsio tua valebit, cum & Presbyterium hoc, & excommunicationem à Deo ordinatam demonstraueris.
units.tr: of God by the eldership. You are not unaware of what follows. Who has ever been an excommunicator (whether bishop or presbyter) who wished to appear to have acted unjustly? And who, I ask you, would complain of an injury? Would not such a man at once be regarded as contumacious, and be counted by those censors as a despiser of the divine order? But, as I said, your reply will hold good, when you have shown both that this eldership exists and that excommunication was ordained by God.

units.la: Tertium. Is solus ex Ecclesia (sic videlicet vt salus auferatur eiecto) exturbare potest, qui corda intuetur. At hoc non possunt homines. Amplius ergo facere nihil possunt, quàm Sacramentis interdicere. Respondes, concedimus Antecedens, & id negamus contra eos facere, qui vt Dei Ministri agunt, ex ipsius verbo quicquid agunt: imo fideles Domini ministri sumus, quum quos ipse verbo suo ligari vel soluí in coelis declarat, ligatos vel solutos pronunciamus in terris: hàncque in terris factam promulgationem ratam esse in coelis affirmanti Christo credimus. Quorsum haec? Non hoc quaerit argumentum, an, quos Deus verbo suo declarat ligatos aut solutos in coelis, in terris pronunciandi sint soluti aut ligati? & an haec promulgatio rata sit in coelis? sed hoc quaerit, an sic homines possint ex Ecclesia eijcere, vt salutem abscindant? vt argumentum refutes, haec te probare oportebit. Primum quidem, sententiam Dei in coelo ligantis & soluentis non posse hic in terris ex verbo eius declarari & pronuntiari ab alijs, quàm à Conciliabulo Presbyterorum. Nam sacrae literae docent, hanc ex verbo Dei declarationem à quolibet Ministro adeóque priuato, cum res postulat, fieri posse ac debere. Hoc cum negari non possit ab eo, qui sacras literas concedit non solis Presbyteris scriptas esse, probandum tibi erit secundo, Declarationem hanc à Presbyteris factam valere; ab alio quolibet factâ non valere. Tertiò, Deum praecepisse confessum talem eligi, qui coacto concilio consentientibus suffragijs solenniter denuntiet ac promulget Dei sententiā in Coelis factam. Magistratum in scripturis institutum reperio, quid de scelerebus cognoscat ac puniat. Presbyterio vestro hanc datam potestatem sub pio magistratu nusquam legi. Quartò, Deum nollequenquam inuisibilis Ecclesiae consortio viuere, qui non sit membrum internae quoq; Ecclesiae. Suprà ostensum est, multos à Deo in coelis repudiari, quos tamen in externa communione in terris ferat. Quinetiam κ᾽ ἀνιάτ, καὶ ἀπρίατ operantes, quos se fatetur non cognouisse, non tantum tolerat in Ecclesia, & coram se epulari ac bibere finit, verumetiam donis expellendi Daemonia aliáq; miracula faciendi ornat. Matt. 7. & Lucae 13. Quintò, hanc diuini iudicij renunciationem & interpretationē idē esse cum interdictione Sacramentorū. Sextò, promulgationem sententiæ à Deo latae in coelis idem esse cum eiectione ex Ecclesiae visibilis societate. At hanc non esse idem cum illa, & per se notum est, & ex dictis tuis constat, qui hanc ex illa colligi supra dixeris. Haec, inquam, cum ex scripturis euidenter probaueris, argumentum te nostrum refutauisse fatebor: nunc te ad rem attinens nihil respondisse libere dico.
units.tr: Third. He alone can cast someone out of the Church (so that salvation is taken away from the one cast out) who sees into the hearts. But men cannot do this. Therefore they can do nothing more than forbid the sacraments. You reply: we grant the antecedent, and we deny that we act against those who, as ministers of God, do whatever they do from his own Word. Indeed we are faithful ministers of the Lord, since, when he declares that those whom he binds or looses by his word are bound or loosed in heaven, we pronounce them bound or loosed on earth; and we believe Christ, who affirms that the proclamation made on earth is ratified in heaven. Why these things? The argument does not ask whether those whom God declares by his word to be bound or loosed in heaven are to be pronounced loosed or bound on earth, nor whether this proclamation is ratified in heaven. It asks this: whether men can in this way cast someone out of the Church so as to cut off his salvation. To refute the argument you will have to prove these things. First, that God's sentence binding and loosing in heaven cannot be declared and pronounced here on earth from the Word of God by anyone other than the assembly of elders. For the sacred letters teach that this declaration from the Word of God can and must be made by any minister, and so by a private person, when the matter demands it. Since this cannot be denied by one who grants that the sacred letters were written not for the elders alone, you will have to prove secondly that a declaration made by the elders is valid, and that one made by anyone else is not valid. Thirdly, that God commanded that a confessed person be chosen who, with a council assembled and by consenting votes, solemnly announces and promulgates God's sentence made in heaven. I find that the magistrate is instituted in the Scriptures to inquire into and punish crimes. Nowhere do I read that this power has been given to your eldership under a godly magistrate. Fourthly, that God does not wish anyone to live in fellowship with the invisible Church who is not a member of the inward Church as well. It has been shown above that many are rejected by God in heaven, whom nevertheless he bears in outward communion on earth. Moreover, those who work [κ᾽ ἀνιάτ, καὶ ἀπρίατ], whom he confesses he never knew, he not only tolerates in the Church and allows to feast and drink in his presence, but even endows with the gift of casting out demons and working miracles. Matt. 7. and Luke 13. Fifthly, that this announcement and interpretation of the divine judgment is the same as the interdiction of the sacraments. Sixthly, that the promulgation of a sentence passed by God in heaven is the same as expulsion from the fellowship of the visible Church. But that this is not the same as that is both self-evident and clear from what you yourself have said, since you have stated above that the former is inferred from the latter. When you have clearly proved these things from the Scriptures, I will confess that you have refuted our argument; as things stand, I say frankly that you have answered nothing relevant to the matter.

units.la: Quartum argumentum. Apostoli eos qui fidem retinuerunt, & Christianam doctrinam non vituperarunt ac profciderunt, propter admissa flagitia non condemnarunt eiectione ex Ecclesia, extra quam salus nulla fit, sed corporalibus quosdam ex his poenis affecerunt. Ad hoc respondendo quaeris, an exiftimam Petrum, quum à manuum impositione Simonem Magum repulisset, eundē ad κοινωνίαν corporis Domini nisi manifeste resipiscentem, admissorum fuisse? Et qui ob animi peruersitatem, addis, sic repellitur à Spiritu Sancti donis, vt dicatur nec partem, nec fortem habere in Euangelij praedicatione, qui tandem ad mensam Domini, nisi refipiscentiam testatus, admitti potuit? Iterum nihil ad argumentum respondes.
units.tr: Fourth argument. The apostles did not condemn by expulsion from the Church, outside of which there is no salvation, those who kept the faith and did not disparage or abandon Christian doctrine, on account of the sins they had committed; rather they subjected some of them to bodily punishments. In answering this you ask whether I think that Peter, when he had driven Simon the Magician away from the laying on of hands, would have admitted him to the communion of the Lord's body unless he showed clear repentance? And you add that he who, because of the perversity of his mind, is so repelled from the gifts of the Holy Spirit that he is said to have neither part nor lot in the preaching of the gospel, could he finally have been admitted to the Lord's table without a profession of repentance? Again you answer nothing to the argument.

units.la: Quoniam longè aliud fuit manuum impositione Spiritum Sanctum, siue donum edendi miracula donare, & vsum Sacramentorum permittere. Sanè Samaritani, de quibus in hoc 8. Act. cap. agitur, Christiani fuerunt facti ac baptizati, priusquam ad eos Petrus & Iohannes descendissent, vt impositis manibus virtute miracula edendi supernè ornarentur. Omnes Sacramentis vti oportuit, qui se Christianos esse profiterentur: at non omnes miraculis clarere oportuit, 1.Cor. 12. Videtur hoc donum ferè solis Apostolis, aut certè non multis aliis à Deo concessum, vt manuum impositione Spiritussancti vim praedictam hominibus impetrarent. Post Apostolos ceremonia tantum videtur fuisse, qua certi quidam in munere aliquo confirmarentur. Paulus certè hortatur Timotheum, ne facilè vlli manus imponat 1. Tim. 5. Quocirca non sequitur, negata huic fuit manuum impositio. Ergo non est ad Sacramenta admissus. Itaq; nihil hoc exemplo probas.
units.tr: For the laying on of hands to bestow the Holy Spirit, or the gift of working miracles, is something quite different from permitting the use of the sacraments. Indeed the Samaritans, of whom Acts 8 treats, were made Christians and baptized before Peter and John came down to them, so that by the laying on of hands they might be adorned from above with the power of working miracles. All who professed to be Christians had to use the sacraments; but not all had to shine with miracles, 1 Cor. 12. This gift seems to have been granted almost only to the apostles, or certainly to not many others by God, so that by the laying on of hands they could obtain for men the power mentioned of the Holy Spirit. After the apostles the ceremony seems to have been only one by which certain persons were confirmed in some office. Paul certainly exhorts Timothy not to lay hands easily on anyone, 1 Tim. 5. Therefore it does not follow that because the laying on of hands was denied to someone, he was therefore not admitted to the sacraments. So you prove nothing by this example.

units.la: At excipies ac dices, Simonem Magum nec partem nec sortem habuisse in praedicatione Euangelij. Respondeo tantò minus seruire tibi eius exemplum posse. Nos enim de illis loquimur, qui doctrinam veritatis perceperunt ac tenent: quam Magum non tenuisse aut non retinuisse hoc satis probat, quod argento Spiritussancti dona comparari opinatus est: quodque non pro se petiuit, sed vt alijs, (accepta pecunia) dare iterum posset. Item quod Petrus dicit se videre in eo mentem non rectam coram Deo, sed plenam felle amarissimo, & sceleribus irretitam. An & vos hoc pacto hominum animos repentè iudicare potestis? Deinde non scribit Lucas Petrum ad Magum dixisse, eum partem nullam habere in Euangelij praedicatione, sed in eo, de quo agebatur. Mox enim hortatur ad poenitentiam, quod tuae aduersatur oppositioni. Praeterea loquimur nos de illis, qui Sacramentis vti cupiunt, non de contemnentibus, aut non satis digne de eisdem sentientibus. Quod si doctrinam retinuisset Magus, atq; verbis primum, deinde etiam Coene petitione dolorem suum testatus fuisset, (vt cum baptizatus est fidem testatus fuit) non audeo dicere Petrum Caenam ei negaturum fuisse. Equidem hortatur eum ad refipiscentiam & ad preces, an forte Deus illi remittere peccatum vellet. Quicquid de hoc fit, de quo neque ego, neque tu, certi aliquid dicere possumus, constat exemplum non aduersari nostræ sententiæ, sed tuę definitioni: quæ ponit excommunicationem esse sententiam Presbyteris in nomine Domini congregatis pronunciatam: quale hîc nihil factum legimus. Hoc legimus, Petrum, Deo nimirum ipsi hoc reuelante, ex vna ista Magi petitione mentem eius praeuam cognouisse, quam Philippus ante, cui tamen semper adhaeserat, cognouisse non legitur. Multa donauit Deus Apostolis, quae perperam alijs quoque tributa putemus.
units.tr: But you will object and say that Simon Magus had neither part nor lot in the preaching of the gospel. I answer that his example can serve your purpose all the less. For we are speaking of those who have received and hold the doctrine of truth. That Magus did not hold or retain it is sufficiently shown by the fact that he supposed the gifts of the Holy Spirit could be bought with silver, and that he sought them not for himself but so that he might be able to give them to others for money. Likewise, Peter says that he sees in him a heart not right before God, but full of bitter gall and entangled in wickedness. Can you too judge men's hearts so hastily in this way? Next, Luke does not write that Peter told Magus he had no part in the preaching of the gospel, but that he had no part in the matter under discussion. Peter goes on at once to urge him to repentance, which is opposed to your position. Moreover, we are speaking of those who desire to partake of the sacraments, not of those who despise them or think of them without sufficient reverence. But if Magus had retained the doctrine, and had shown his sorrow by his words and then also by asking for the Lord's Supper, just as he showed his faith when he was baptized, I do not dare to say that Peter would have refused him the Supper. Indeed, Peter urges him to repentance and to prayer, in case God perhaps wished to forgive him his sin. Whatever becomes of this, about which neither I nor you can say anything for certain, it is clear that the example does not oppose our opinion but your definition, which holds that excommunication is a sentence pronounced by the elders gathered in the name of the Lord. We read of nothing like that being done here. We read that Peter, God surely revealing it to him, recognised from that one request of Magus his wicked mind, which Philip had not recognised before, though Magus had always been attached to him. God gave the Apostles many gifts, which we should not wrongly attribute to others as well.

units.la: Quintum argumentum. Aliqui ex peccatoribus excommunicatis sub vitæ finem demum resipuerunt, piéque mortui sunt. Ergo cum ex Ecclesia expulsus aliquis dicitur, è societate externa, non interna & spirituali, eiectus, esse dicitur. Sensus est, cum constet aliquos moriturôs demum resipuisse, piéque in Domino occubuisse, constat illud etiam, tales, si ab Ecclesia reiecti cogitentur, non fuisse à spirituali Christi societate expulsos. Non enim fuissent seruati. Ad hoc respondes. Antecedens concedimus, consequens negamus. Etsi enim intelligere homines non possunt, quibus videlicet & quo momento Deus sit daturus refipiscentiæ spiritum, tamen ea res nihil officit ordinario Ministerio: quo iubentur oues pascere, tum famelicas ad pabulum deducendo, tum aberrantes, si patiantur, blandè, sin minus periculi denunciatione & pabuli moderata subductione, in viam reducendo.
units.tr: Fifth argument. Some excommunicated sinners at the end of their lives did at last repent, and died piously. Therefore, when someone is said to be expelled from the Church, he is to be understood as cast out from the external fellowship, not from the internal and spiritual one. The sense is this: since it is certain that some who were about to die did at last repent and fell asleep piously in the Lord, it is also certain that such people, if they are thought to have been cast out by the Church, were not expelled from the spiritual fellowship of Christ. For otherwise they would not have been saved. To this you reply: we grant the antecedent, but deny the consequent. For although men cannot know to whom and at what moment God will give the spirit of repentance, that matter does not hinder the ordinary ministry, by which the ministers are commanded to feed the sheep: by leading the hungry ones to pasture, and by bringing back the straying ones, if they allow it, gently, or if not, by warning them of danger and by moderately withdrawing the pasture.

units.la: Si per subductionem pabuli intelligis verbi aut Sacramentorum negationem, de tuo hoc dicis, non loqueris cum scripturis, quæ nusquam iubent pabula haec subducere. Venio ad argumentum: Consequens mei argumenti hoc est.
units.tr: If by withdrawing the pasture you mean the denial of the Word or of the sacraments, you say this on your own authority; you are not speaking in agreement with the Scriptures, which nowhere command such pasture to be withdrawn. I come to the argument. The consequence of my argument is this.

units.la: Excommunicato, qui in Domino obdormiuit, per
units.tr: He who in the Lord has fallen asleep, though excommunicated, has

units.la: excommunicationem non fuit adempta seu abscissa salus. Ex hoc deinde sequitur: illum ab externa tantum, non autem interna Christi societate seclusum fuisse: ac proinde excommunicationem non esse definiendam, salutis negatione. Quomodo, quaeso te, consequens negas, quo verius esse nihil potest? Homines non intelligunt, ais, quando Deus sit daturus spiritum resipiscentiae: ac hoc Ministerio non officit. Concedo omnia. Addis deinde: At pastor famelicas oues ad pabulum deducere ( Cur ergo petentibus Sacramenta siue pabulum, tu subducis ac negas? Nos enim de petentibus agere audisti) errantes aut blandè, aut ratione alia licita, (Nam si per subductionem pabuli intelligis negationem Verbi & Sacramentorum, toto erras coelo) reducere debet. Concedo hoc quoque. An propterea, qui in Domino est mortuus, si fuerat excommunicatus, non est saluus? Ipse tu, & recte quidem, adducis verba mea, quibus probare volui excommunicationem non esse abscisione salutis definiendam: ac proinde excusare te non possum: nisi forte idem putaris esse consequens negare, & consequentiam. At hic error nimis crassus foret. Cogita posthac diligentius quid & quomodo respondeas, ne dormiuisse puteris. Consecutionem, quam tu hic non oppugnas, oppugnare autem si scisses, voluisses, puto, breviter probabo. Faciam eo libentius, quod simul etiam responsum erit illis, quae contra sextum & septimum argumentum adfers. Quisquis iudicio Diuino in coelis facto non est prorsus ab interiore & spirituali Christi coniunctione seclusus, is, si excommunicetur, tantum ab externa ecclesiae communione abiungitur, salute non excidit. Ceterum quisquis tandem vere resipiscit (siue cito siue tarde fiat) nunquam fuit a Christi occulta societate omnino auulsus. Talis ergo tametsi excommunicatus esset ab Ecclesia, non prorsus excideret salute sua, hoc est, excommunicatio ei salutem non ademerat. Nisi hoc modo res habeat, irrita erit electio diuina. Periret enim qui electus est ad vitam sempiternam. Penderet eadem ex vita factisque, nostris.
units.tr: not lost or been cut off from salvation by excommunication. From this it then follows that he was shut out only from the external, and not from the internal, fellowship of Christ; and therefore excommunication is not to be defined as the cutting off of salvation. How, I ask you, do you deny the consequence, when nothing could be more true? You say that men do not know when God is going to give the spirit of repentance, and that this does not hinder the ministry. I grant it all. You add then: but the shepherd should lead the hungry sheep to pasture (why then do you withdraw and deny the sacraments or the pasture to those who ask for them? For you have heard that we are speaking of those who ask), and should bring back the straying ones, either gently or by some other lawful means. (For if by withdrawing the pasture you mean denying the Word and the sacraments, you are altogether wrong.) I grant this too. Does it follow that he who has died in the Lord, if he had been excommunicated, is not saved? You yourself, and rightly so, quote my words, by which I wished to prove that excommunication is not to be defined as the cutting off of salvation; and so I cannot excuse you, unless perhaps you think that denying the consequence and denying the consequence are the same thing. But that error would be too gross. Consider more carefully from now on what and how you answer, lest you be thought to have been asleep. I shall briefly prove the consequence, which you do not here oppose; I think you would have wished to oppose it if you had known how. I shall do this the more willingly because the answer will also serve for what you bring against the sixth and seventh arguments. Whoever, by the judgement of God in heaven, has not been altogether cut off from the inner and spiritual union with Christ, is, if he is excommunicated, separated only from the external communion of the Church; he does not fall from salvation. Moreover, whoever at last truly repents (whether it happens early or late) was never wholly torn away from the hidden fellowship of Christ. Such a person, therefore, even if he were excommunicated by the Church, would not utterly lose his salvation; that is, excommunication had not taken salvation away from him. Unless the matter stands in this way, the divine election will be void. For he who has been chosen to eternal life would perish. And salvation would then depend on our life and deeds.

units.la: Falsa esset doctrina de Sanctorum perseuerantia & electione: quam tu infra aperte astruis. Quanquam verò ibi emplastro quodam tegere conaris, nihil tamen efficis apud intelligentes. Et ne hoc quidem excusat, quod non pure, sed cum conditione dicitur ei salus negata fuisse: propterea quod à Deo in coelis abiectus nunquam fuit, quantumuis aliter visum esset hominibus.
units.tr: The doctrine of the perseverance and election of the saints would be false, which you openly set forth below. Although you try to cover it there with a kind of plaster, you accomplish nothing before those who understand. Nor does it excuse you that you say salvation was denied to him not absolutely, but with a condition, on the ground that he was never cast off by God in heaven, however things might seem to men.

units.la: Consideretur exemplum Dauidis, qui multis mensibus in scelere suo haesit. Is, si tunc Excommunicatus fuisset, dum sibi adhuc in facto suo blandiretur, non tamen salute sua excidisset. Illustrius adhuc est exemplum Manassis Regis: quo vix vllus fuit nequior. Is tamen piè creditur mortuus. Quapropter non fuit absolutè simpliciterque à Deo in coelis damnatus. Nec refert vtrum excommunicetur aliquis, an dignus sit Excommunicatione, Idem enim semper iudicat Deus, siue Ecclesia loquatur siue sileat. Certè qui hodie similealiquid faceret, à Presbiteris omninò excluderetur, siue electus esset apud Deum, siue non electus. Quod si electus esset, salutem ei non tollerent sua sententia Presbyteritui.
units.tr: Consider the example of David, who clung to his sin for many months. If he had been excommunicated at that time, while he was still flattering himself in his deed, he would nevertheless not have fallen from his salvation. The example of King Manasseh is more striking still, for hardly anyone was more wicked than he. Yet he is believed to have died piously. Therefore he was not absolutely and simply condemned by God in heaven. Nor does it matter whether someone is excommunicated or only deserves excommunication, for God always judges in the same way, whether the Church speaks or keeps silent. Certainly, anyone who did something similar today would be wholly shut out by the elders, whether or not he was elected with God. But if he were elected, the sentence of the eldership would not take away his salvation.

units.la: Secundò dare alicui salutem, consortium Christi internum, & huius generis alia, an non sunt res spirituales, caelestes, & Diuinæ, quas praeter Deum conferre nobis nulla possit creatura? Sanè ita res habet. Ergo nec auferre talia à nobis possunt homines. Quippe eiusdem potestatis est, dare & auferre haec caelestia donna. Quod etiam homines talia dicuntur dare, ita est accipiendum, vt ex verbo Dei cogitemus foris nuntiare & explicare, quae intus facit Deus, vbi, quando, quantum, quomodo ipse vult. Homo est internus & externus: Minister externus & internus: Ministerium externum & internum: verbum externum & internum: constant etiam Sacramenta rebus externis & internis. Duę ergo sunt σύμβολα seu συμβολαι, vna externorū, altera internorū: quę sine pudedo, & foedo errore confundi permiscerinunquā poterunt. Non sunt etiam sic inter se nexa externa & interna, vt altera sine altero non reperiantur. Non quisquis externè baptizatur aqua, interne abluitur. Non quisquis panem Domini edit, Domini edit. Non quisquis Christum annuntiari audit, Christum induit. Non quisquis salute excidisse pronunciatur ab hominibus, à Deo quoque condemnatur. Non quisquis abvsu Sacramentorum externorum repellitur, re Sacramenti à Deo priuatur. Summa est, homines plantant ac rigant, Deus solus dat incrementum, vbi, quando, quibus, quantum, quomodo, ipsi bonum iudicatur: non quomodo Ministris externis placet.
units.tr: Secondly, to give someone salvation, the inward fellowship of Christ, and other things of this kind, are these not spiritual, heavenly and divine matters, which no creature except God can bestow upon us? Certainly that is so. Therefore men cannot take such things away from us either, for the power to give and to take away these heavenly gifts is of one and the same kind. That men are also said to give such things is to be understood in this way: that we, from the Word of God, announce and explain outwardly what God works inwardly, where, when, how much and how he wills. Man is inward and outward; the minister is outward and inward; the ministry is outward and inward; the word is outward and inward; the sacraments too consist of outward and inward things. There are therefore two tokens [σύμβολα] or signs [συμβολαι], one of outward things and the other of inward things, which can never be confused without shame and foul error. Nor are outward and inward things so bound together that one is not found without the other. Not everyone who is baptized outwardly with water is inwardly washed. Not everyone who eats the Lord's bread eats the Lord. Not everyone who hears Christ proclaimed puts on Christ. Not everyone who is pronounced by men to have fallen from salvation is also condemned by God. Not everyone who is repelled from the outward use of the sacraments is deprived of the reality of the sacrament by God. In short, men plant and water, but God alone gives the increase, where, when, to whom, how much and in what way he judges good; not as it pleases the outward ministers.

units.la: Tertiò, par est potestas ligandi & soluendi, adeò vt qui altera caret, vtraque careat: & qui vnam habet, ambas habeat. Ergo si constiterit, presbyteros in soluendo excommunicatum, non dare salutem, constat etiam eosdem ligando non adimere salutem. Tam autem certum est prius illud, vt Pontificij scholastici id negare ausi non fuerint. Itaque valde se aliqui torquent, vt sacerdotem aliquid amplius facere doceant, dum à Deo prius solutum absoluit, quam quòd in externam Ecclesiæ societatem interim recipit. Tandem post longas concertationes & varias molitiones in eo ipso acquiescunt, internorum bonorum ex eo nihil ei accedere. Hinc aliqui ausi sunt affirmare, Excommunicationem nil esse aliud, quam figmentum presbyterorum: quod ipsimet testificantur. Sit igitur concludo. Qui excommunicatum soluit, non plus ei dat, quam quod permittit eum externæ Ecclesiæ communicare: Ergo qui excommunicat, nihil aliud facit, quam quod prohibet ritibus Ecclesiæ participare.
units.tr: Thirdly, the power of binding and the power of loosing are equal, so that whoever lacks one lacks both, and whoever has one has both. Therefore, if it is established that the elders, in loosing the excommunicated, do not give salvation, it is also established that in binding they do not take salvation away. The former point is so certain that the Papist scholastics have not dared to deny it. Hence some torment themselves greatly to teach that the priest does something more when he absolves one who has already been loosed by God than when he meanwhile admits him into the external fellowship of the Church. In the end, after long contentions and various contrivances, they rest on this very point: that nothing of inner goods accrues to him from it. Hence some have dared to affirm that excommunication is nothing but a figment of the elders, which they themselves bear witness to. Let it therefore be concluded: whoever looses the excommunicated does not give him more than that he permits him to communicate in the external Church. Therefore whoever excommunicates does nothing other than forbid him to take part in the rites of the Church.

units.la: Quartò, contradicis tibi ipse, dum hoc negas. Etenim contendis neminem ritè excommunicari, nisi prius à Deo excommunicatum, adeo vt nisi diuina præcesserit, humana irrita fit & fabulosa. Addis hoc etiam, eam nil aliud esse, quam diuinæ in cœlis factæ promulgationem. Quæ si sunt vera, non tollit salutem humana Excommunicatio, sed declarat solummodò quid Deus hac in parte fecerit in cœlis. Cæterùm indicare quid alius decreuerit aut iudicârit, non est idem illud decernere & & iudicare. Supra exposui, quid interfit inter eos, qui de re aliqua sententiam cum autoritate ferunt, & eos, qui ab alijs latam promulgant. Euidenter igitur probatum à nobis est, excommunicatores amplius nihil facere posse, quàm à Sacramentis arcere: quatenus è societate externa Ecclesiae dicuntur aliquos eijcere. Quocirca facilè se tutabitur argumentum nostrum aduersus tuas reprehensiones.
units.tr: Fourthly, you contradict yourself when you deny this. For you contend that no one is rightly excommunicated unless he has first been excommunicated by God, so that, unless a divine sentence has gone before, the human one is void and fabulous. You add also that it is nothing other than the promulgation of what has been done by God in heaven. If these things are true, human excommunication does not take away salvation, but only declares what God has done in this matter in heaven. Moreover, to indicate what another has decided or judged is not the same as to decide and judge that thing oneself. I set out above what difference there is between those who pronounce a judgment on some matter with authority and those who promulgate one passed by others. It has therefore been clearly proved by us that excommunicators can do no more than keep men from the sacraments, insofar as they are said to cast someone out of the external fellowship of the Church. Wherefore our argument will easily defend itself against your rebukes.

units.la: Addam his testimonium D. Lutheri, qui in sermone de excommunicatione Tomo German. 1. folio 239. haec habet. Excommunicare non est, vt quidam opinantur, animam Satanae tradere, & precum fructu à pijs factarum spoliare. Nam vbi vera fides & charitas in corde remanent, etiam vera communio Dei, vt precum Christianitatis fructus permanent: postquam aliud est excommunicatio, nec fieri aliud potest, quàm priuatio externi Sacramenti aut commercij cum hominibus: ac si in custodiam traditus externa amicorum consuetudine priuer, amore & fauore eorundem interea non spolier. Audis hic excommunicationem non damnare, aut interiorem communionem nobis Christi & Ecclesiae inuisibilis adimere, sed ab externa tantum societate excludere? Audis etiam eam nec aliud esse, nec aliud fieri posse, quàm externi sacramenti seu visibilis signi (commercij negationem hùc non pertinere firmè probatum videbis, si nostra perlegeris) spoliationem: Si ergo rem interna m & coelestem, corpus Christi pro nobis crucifixum, nobis non eripit, quo pacto salutem abscindit? Non cito D. Lutheri testimonia, vt mea cis probem, sed vt videas adeo esse aperta & clara, quae dico, vt neminem Theologum latere debeant.
units.tr: I will add to these the testimony of Dr Luther, who in his sermon on excommunication (Tomo German. 1, folio 239) has the following: "To excommunicate is not, as some suppose, to hand over the soul to Satan and to strip it of the fruit of prayers offered by the godly. For where true faith and love remain in the heart, the true communion of God also remains, as do the fruits of Christian prayers. Excommunication is one thing; nor can it be anything other than the deprivation of the external sacrament or of dealings with men, just as if someone handed over to custody were deprived of the external company of friends but were not meanwhile stripped of their love and favour." Do you hear here that excommunication does not condemn, nor take from us inner communion with Christ and the invisible Church, but only excludes from external fellowship? Do you hear also that it is neither anything else nor can be anything else than the deprivation of the external sacrament or visible sign? (You will see it firmly proved that the denial of commerce does not pertain here, if you read our work through.) If, then, it does not snatch from us the inner and heavenly thing, the body of Christ crucified for us, in what way does it cut off salvation? I do not cite the testimonies of Dr Luther to prove my case, but so that you may see that what I say is so open and clear that no theologian should be ignorant of it.

units.la: Quod deinceps carpere videris, quod Ministrorum actiones externum quid esse dico, quàm sit incongruum ex recitatis facilè potest perspici. Verba tua sunt. Hanc piam & ab ipso Deo gregis sui gubernatoribus praescriptam solicitudinem (scilicet oues famelicas ad pabulum deducendi, errantesq; in viam reuocandi) externũ quiddam esse quàm diu voles, arbitraberis, Ego adhuc putaui Ministrum externum, externum verbum, & externa signa, externo offerri homini, nunc verò videor mihi videre, vos externis non velle contentos esse: tamen si in responsione sponsione ad 3. argumentum scripseris, vos vsqueadeo amentes, aut impios non esse, vt, quod vnius Dei est, vobis arrogetis. Hoc si verum est, quid mihi succenses, quod excommunicatores salutem nulli praescindere posse affirmo, sed externa solum agere contendo? An salutem dare non ex illis est, quae vnius sunt Dei, nullius creaturae? Dicis legitima veri presbyterij iudicia non secus formidanda, quam si ex ore suo pronunciasset Christus. Idem nos etiam arbitramur: sed tuum illud presbyterium nondum probasti a Deo ordinatum: nec ostendisti iudicia haec, de quibus inter nos disputamus, esse Dei verbo consentanea. Quare dicis tantum multa, sed probas pauca. Sic cum a sacramentis prohibitum, a re quoque sacramenti, id est, Christi communione prohiberi asseris, absque scripturis loqueris: At hoc modo loquenti tibi fidem non habemus: imo quod vnius Dei est, imprudenter te hominibus tribuere affirmamus.
units.tr: As to what you go on to carp at, that I call the actions of the ministers something external, how incongruous this is can easily be seen from what has been quoted. Your words are: "This pious solicitude, prescribed by God himself to the governors of his flock (namely, to lead the hungry sheep to pasture and to recall the wandering to the way), you will think to be something external for as long as you like." I had thought until now that the external minister, the external word and the external signs are offered to an external man; but now I seem to see that you are not willing to be content with external things. Yet if in your reply to my third argument you have written that you are not so mad or impious as to arrogate to yourselves what belongs to God alone, then why do you blame me, if this is true, because I affirm that excommunicators cannot cut off salvation from anyone, but contend that they do only external things? Or is giving salvation not among those things which belong to the one God and to no creature? You say that the lawful judgments of a true eldership are to be feared no less than if Christ had pronounced them from his own mouth. We think the same; but you have not yet proved that your eldership has been ordained by God, nor have you shown that these judgments, about which we dispute among ourselves, agree with the Word of God. So you say many things, but prove few. Thus, when you assert that one who is forbidden the sacraments is also forbidden the thing of the sacrament, that is, communion with Christ, you speak without Scripture; and we do not put faith in you when you speak in this way. Indeed, we affirm that you imprudently attribute to men what belongs to God alone.

units.la: Cap. II. De Gradibus seu partibus Excommunicationis.
units.tr: Chapter II. On the Degrees or Parts of Excommunication.

units.la: NOstram definitionem bonam & concinnè constitutam: tuam autem ingentibus erroribus refertam demonstrauimus, nunc quid in partitione nostra accuses consideremus. Primum est, nos perperam duos gradus excommunicationis posuisse: cum tres sint apud vos ecclesiasticae censurae gradus. Ego neq; quot apud alios, neque quot apud vos sint censurae ecclesiasticae species & gradus quaerendum mihi vnquam putaui: sed hoc solum inuestigare propositum habui, quot essent excommunicationis gradus. Huius duos esse apud vos inueni: & duos etiam apud Pontificios: quanquam alia ratione hi duos faciant. Supra ex tuismet verbis duos esse ostendi. Commonefactionem & multam inter excommunicationis gradus collocare non debui, cùm, qui eo modo inrepaturaut multatur, non putetur ab vllo priuatus communione fidelium. At cui sacramentorum vsu interdicitur, is iam pro abiuncto à plerisque omnibus habetur. Proinde nec hic quidem iustam vllam causam habuisti contradicendi. Asseris non meminisse te plures duobus, excommunicatos intra decennium, mulierem, & foeneratorem. Aut igitur Iohannes Morellus anno 63. à vobis excommunicatus, ille foenerator fuit: aut in scripto Magistratus continente sententiam de exustione libri, causa haec omissa fuit. Mirarer si tam splendidi & luculenti actus tam cito potuisses obliuisci. Sed ad rem nostram.
units.tr: Our definition we have shown to be good and well put together, while yours is crammed with huge errors. Now let us consider what you find fault with in our division. First, you say we wrongly posited two degrees of excommunication, since among you there are three degrees of ecclesiastical censure. I never thought it my task to ask how many kinds and degrees of ecclesiastical censure there are among other churches or among you. My only aim was to investigate how many degrees of excommunication there are. I have found two among you, and two among the Papists too, though these two count them on a different principle. Above, I showed from your own words that there are two. I ought not to have placed admonition and fine among the degrees of excommunication, since a person who is punished with a fine for a fault is not thought to be cut off from the fellowship of the faithful by anyone. But the one who is forbidden the use of the sacraments is already regarded by most people as cut off. So here too you had no just reason for contradicting me. You assert that you do not remember more than two persons excommunicated within ten years, a woman and a moneylender. Either John Morellus, who was excommunicated by you in the year 63, was the moneylender, or else the sentence of the magistrate concerning the burning of the book, which contains this matter, left it out. I would be surprised if you could have forgotten such splendid and famous deeds so quickly. But to our business.

units.la: Pontificios dixi haud recte introduxisse excommunicationem maiorem, quae ab omni licito actu excludit. Hanc tu, tametsi ea non vtamini, non simpliciter damnandam censes, cum expresso Dei verbo nitatur. Arbitror tibi nondum excidisse, me de excommunicatione illorum agere. Qui doctrinam approbant, & tantum non viuunt, quomodo Christianos decet. Iam videamus tuas rationes.
units.tr: I said that the Papists wrongly introduced the greater excommunication, which shuts a person out from every lawful act. You, although you do not use it, do not think it should be simply condemned, since it rests on the express word of God. I suppose it has not yet slipped your mind that I am speaking of their excommunication, of those who approve the doctrine and scarcely live as Christians ought to live. Now let us look at your arguments.

units.la: ARGVMENTVM I.
units.tr: ARGUMENT I.

units.la: Immundos, ais, ab ipso templi aditu prohibitos fuisse, non inficiaberis. Et cum excipis hoc externum quiddam fuisse, nihil nobis quidem dicere videris, quod contra te non faciat, vt alibi nos ostensuros speramus. Alterutrum enim fatearis oportet, vel detestabiliorem fuisse coram Deo externam, quàm intrinsecam pollutionem, vel hac, quàm illa, pollutos, etiam habitos fuisse impuriores. Respondeo, me non inficiari quidem, quin ab aditu templi prohibiti fuerint immundi: (hoc enim scriptura testatur) Sed ex hoc sequi, quod tu vis, nempe propter vitam improbe actam arcendum aliquem nunc esse à sacris ritibus, constanter nego: & quidem iis permotus rationibus, quas tibi facilius sit contemnere, quàm refellere. Verùm de hac re copiosè disseremus, cum huc nos tu, sicut promittis, retrahes: in praesentia breuiter tantum indicabo, cuiusmodi argumentator sis. Argumento ab immundis sub lege ducto vis ostendere excommunicationem maiorem, quæ actum omnem licitum prohibet, atque excommunicatum æternæ damnationi addicit, niti scripturis. An immundi sub lege pro damnatis habebantur? An ab omni actu licito prohibebantur? An ab omnibus Sacramentis arcebantur? Non ita habet. Etiamsi immundus aliquis moreretur, de eius tamen salute ob id nullus dubitabat, cum sanctissimus quisque sic mori posset nempe Gonorrhoea laborans, apud mortuū cubans. Item mulier aut menstruis, aut profluvio altero ægrotans, aut leprosus. An non Sacramentum expiationis sub poena exitij cogebantur etiam immundi lugendo celebrare? An non Sabbatha tenebantur observare? Sed de his postea: nunc tua expendamus. Non recordor me sic argumentatum, quia videlicet legalis immunditia externum quiddam fuerit, non potuisse eam significare impuritatem vitæ morumque. Argumentum in hoc loco tuum talis videtur esse. Sceleribus polluti impuriores erant pollutis sub lege. Ergo cum hi arcerentur à sacris ritibus, multo magis vitijs contaminati repellendi fuerunt. Si eadem poena, & non diuersis affici Deus iussisset utrosque, consequeretur certe impuriores magis prohibendos à templo fuisse minus impuris. Similis tua est ratiocinatio huic, ut postea clarissimè perspicietur: Carbonario vel alio quopiam homine sordido, qui sua sorde tangentes inquinet, impurior est ebriosus, fur, aut homicida: Ergo mundis induti vestibus homines multo magis furem fugient, ne contactu eius vestes suas contaminent, quam Carbonarium. Certe ut vestibus caveamus, magis fugimus Carbonarium vestes habentem carbonum puluere oppletas, quam furem mundis vestitum indumentis. Porro similia esse hæc argumenta postea euidentissimè demonstrabo.
units.tr: You say that the unclean were forbidden access to the very entrance of the temple, and you will not deny it. And when you add that this was something external, you seem to say nothing to us that does not tell against you, as we hope to show elsewhere. For you must admit one of two things: either external pollution was more detestable before God than internal, or those polluted in the former way were considered more impure than those polluted in the latter. I reply that I do not deny that the unclean were barred from the entrance to the temple (for Scripture bears witness to this). But I flatly deny that it follows, as you wish, that someone must now be kept from the sacred rites on account of a wicked life. I deny it for reasons that you will find easier to despise than to refute. Yet we shall discuss this matter at length when you draw us back to it, as you promise. For the present I will only briefly point out what sort of arguer you are.
