Do these things not contradict each other: that no one who desires it is prevented, and yet that the judgment rests with others, whether he desires it rightly and truly? And who, I ask you, can make a lawful use of your excommunication, which was devised by men without the Word of God? Men abuse divine institutions. Will you make lawful use of a human decree, which you thrust upon us with such contention of minds as if it were divine law? Or do men not err in judging only among the Allobroges? Likewise, who wrote that one seeking the sacraments must declare his desire properly to the elders, that is, as it seems right to them? As to your denial that excommunication is exclusion from the Supper alone, but a declaration of exclusion from the kingdom of heaven, this was refuted above, sufficiently and more than sufficiently, together with the other points related here.

units.la: Multos apud veteres fuisse scripsi, qui ad finem vitæ demum baptizati fuerint, quos tamen ob id nullus putauerit Satanæ traditos. Cum ergo, inquam, nullibi scriptum sit illum damnandum qui à Coena cessactus abstineat, non illum, qui baptismum volens differat: cur illi potius, quàm hi, exiſtimantur Satanæ traditi? An melior est, qui vltrò à baptismo abstinet, eo, qui coenam desiderat, sed à presbyteris arcetur? Ad hæc, quæ in primo scripto obiter mihi notarem, in Thesibus repetere non volui, sic respondes, vt socordiam veterum hac in parte accuses: quos ego in præsentia neque defendere, neque accusare decreui. Tradi Satanæ aliud fuisse apud Apostolum, quàm vel baptismum deferre, vel vltrò à Coena abstinere tibi perlibenter concedo. Aut nescis quid voluerim dicere, aut nescire te simulas. Nunquam enim vel dixi vel somniaui, hæc non toto coelo, quod aiunt, differre.
units.tr: I wrote that there were many among the ancients who were baptized only at the end of their lives, yet no one therefore thought them delivered to Satan. Since, I say, nowhere is it written that the one who abstains from the Supper through neglect is to be damned, nor the one who wishes to defer baptism, why are these rather than those thought to be delivered to Satan? Or is he better off who voluntarily abstains from baptism than he who desires the Supper but is kept back by the elders? To these points, which I had noted only in passing in my first writing and did not wish to repeat in the Theses, you reply in such a way as to accuse the sloth of the ancients in this respect; I have decided neither to defend nor to accuse them at present. That being delivered to Satan meant something other for the Apostle than either withholding baptism or voluntarily abstaining from the Supper, I readily grant you. Either you do not know what I meant, or you pretend not to know. For I never said or dreamed that these things do not differ by the whole heaven, as the saying goes.

units.la: Supra, cum propositum esset probare, Apostolos nullum excommunicauisse, argumentum, quod hoc loco tu recitas, proposui his fermè verbis. Neque rixosos, neque schismatis authores, neque in ipsa Coenæ celebratione Ebrios factos, neque inflatos illos Gnosticos, neque mortuorum resurrectionem negantes, neque alioqui dissolutè viuentes ab vsu Coenæ iussit separari: cum minora tamen cortigat, vt quod domi suæ quisque cibum capere debeat. Mandat vt vnusquisque seipsum probet: non præcipit, vt alij alios probent. Monet, vt omnes studeant digne accedere, ne sibi iudicium edant: non iubet quenquam emanere; tamețsi indignè vescentibus castigationem Domini denunciet. In 2. deinde Epist. cap. 12. & 13. illis, quos post admonitionem non poenituerat immunditiæ, libidinis, & impudicitiæ, quam patrauerat, non minatur amotionem à mensa Domini: sed pro autoritate ac potestate sibi à Deo tradita rigidè ac duriter se in tales animaduersurum ostendit: quod in suis scriptis frequenter ab eo factum obseruauimus: nunquam verò inuenimus eum à Sacramentis quempiam absterruisse, vel Presbyteris aliisue vllis, hoc vt facerent, imposuisse. Contra hæc quid tu adfers?
units.tr: Above, when the purpose was to prove that the Apostles excommunicated no one, I put forward an argument, which you recite in this place, in roughly these words. He did not order to be separated from the use of the Supper those who were quarrelsome, the authors of schism, those who got drunk at the very celebration of the Supper, those puffed-up Gnostics, those who denied the resurrection of the dead, or those otherwise living dissolutely, although he corrects lesser faults, such as that each person should eat his food at home. He commands that each one prove himself; he does not command that others prove others. He advises that all strive to come worthily, lest they bring judgment on themselves; he does not order anyone to be expelled, although he announces the Lord's chastisement to those who eat unworthily. Then, in the second Epistle, chapters 12 and 13, he does not threaten removal from the Lord's table those who, after admonition, did not repent of the impurity, lust and immodesty they had committed; rather, by the authority and power given him by God, he shows that he will act against such people strictly and harshly. We have observed that he frequently did this in his writings, but we have never found him to have frightened anyone away from the sacraments, or to have imposed on the elders or anyone else that they should do so. What do you bring against these points?

units.la: Nenos quidem ad extrema statim remedia prosilimus, sed omnia prius experienda docemus. Illos verò, qui in Idolæo deinceps vescerentur, censuisse Apostolum dignos, qui arcerentur à mensa Domini, suo loco ostendimus. Capite quinto autem docuit, quod cum cæteris fieri vellet, vetans vel cibum cum ipsis (præeunte legitimo Ecclesiæ iudicio damnatis) sumere. Id enim priuatorum arbitrio relinquere, & periculosum nimis, & toti Ecclesiæ damnosum fuisset. Quo in loco ostendisti Paulum censuisse illos excommunicandos esse, qui Idolothytis vesci pergerent? Supra declaraui te id ita probasse, vt in hoc tuo scripto probas vniuersa: rationibus videlicet nullis, aut tuam ipsius sententiam euertentibus.
units.tr: We indeed do not rush at once to the extreme remedies, but teach that all other means must be tried first. As for those who afterwards ate in the idol temple, we showed in its place that the Apostle judged them worthy to be kept from the Lord's table. In chapter five, however, he taught that he wished the same done to them as to the others, forbidding even eating with them (those already condemned by the lawful judgment of the Church going before). For to leave this to private judgment would have been both far too dangerous and damaging to the whole Church. In what place have you shown that Paul judged those who kept on eating idol meats to be excommunicated? Above, I declared that you proved this as you prove everything in this writing: that is, by no arguments, or by arguments that overturn your own opinion.

units.la: Quantum differant priuati commercij negatio & Sacramentorum interdictio seu excommunicatio supra copiose exposui. Quibus tu probabis hominibus, nisi plane rudissimis, hoc quod Apostolus de fuga priuati conuictus & familiaritatis præcipit, non pertinere ad priuatos quoslibet, seu non esse in priuatorum arbitrio priusquam Presbyteri sua sententia declarauerint hoc faciendum? Næ tu homo es cordatus, qui scripturas interpretari quomodo libet audes: nulla certa expositionis tuæ causa prolata. Textus ipse, verba, res, consilium Apostoli, docent, eùm mandare singulis, quid facere conueniat: nec velle, vt iudicium quoddam Presbyterorum vestrorum, quos ignorauit, exspectent. Falsum est, Ecclesiæ periculosum ac damnosum hoc esse posse: quia spiritussanctus aliter censuit.
units.tr: How far the denial of private intercourse differs from the interdiction or excommunication of the sacraments I have set out fully above. To what people will you prove that what the Apostle commands about flight from private company and familiarity does not pertain to private persons at all, or that it is not in private persons' power before the elders have declared by their sentence that this must be done? Indeed, you are a shrewd fellow, who dares to interpret the Scriptures however he likes, without offering any sure reason for your exposition. The text itself, the words, the matter and the counsel of the Apostle teach that he commands each person what it is fitting to do, nor does he wish them to wait for some judgment of your elders, whom he did not know. It is false that this could be dangerous and damaging to the Church, because the Holy Spirit judged otherwise.

units.la: Alij quidem Corinthios infirmitate sic peccauisse aiunt: ac proinde à Paulo non debuisse priusquam admoniti fuissent excommunicari. His ego sic ante hoc tempus respondi. Quomodo infirmi fuerunt, qui se plus Apostolo scire gloriabantur, illiqué se in rebus omnibus ferè præferebant? An non ideo Gnostici nominati sunt, quod se solos Religionem recte percepisse existimarent, atque idolothytis absque culpa vesci posse putarent, aliisque præterea contra Pauli doctrinam persuadere studerent? Quis credat illos magni æstimauisse Pauli reprehensiones, qui ei modis omnibus obtrectabant, ipsiusque authoritatem superbissimè cleuabant, negligebant, despiciebant? Hi vel non legerunt, vel certè data opera dissimulauerunt, quæ postea sequuntur in Thesibus ex fine cap. 12. & principio 13. secundæ Epistolæ desumpta. Vidissent enim multos ne post admonitionem quidem destitisse à libidine & immunditia sua, quos tamen non iussit excommunicari: quamuis pro potestate sibi, non alijs, à Deo tradita, se acturum contra tales minetur. An non fuerant isti tales in priore Epistola & alias quoque, vt ex textu apparet, admoniti? Inanissima igitur est hæc quoque responsio.
units.tr: Others indeed say that the Corinthians sinned through weakness, and that therefore Paul ought not to have excommunicated them before they had been admonished. To these I have responded thus before this time. How were they weak, who boasted that they knew more than the Apostle, and almost set themselves above him in all things? Were not the Gnostics so named because they thought that they alone had rightly received the religion, and believed that they could eat idol meats without fault, and also strove to persuade others against Paul's teaching? Who would believe that they esteemed Paul's rebukes highly, when they disparaged him in every way and most arrogantly exalted, neglected and despised his authority? These either did not read, or certainly deliberately ignored, what follows later in the Theses, taken from the end of chapter 12 and the beginning of chapter 13 of the second Epistle. For they would have seen that many did not desist from their lust and impurity even after admonition, and yet he did not order those people to be excommunicated, although he threatens that he will act against such people by the power given to him by God, and not to others. Were these not such people, admonished in the former Epistle and elsewhere as well, as appears from the text? This response too is therefore most empty.

units.la: Carpis & hoc, quod dixi, vel tunc irrepsisse interdictionem vsus Sacramentorum in Ecclesiam, cum salutem eis adscribere homines cœperunt: vel certè ex hoc errore prognatam fuisse. Huius somnij mei, vt tu vocas, cum probationem peteres, ipse credo, somniabas. An non res ipsa docet, vt probationis alius non egeat? Expende modo, & assentieris. An non tamen probaui satis, quantum res talis probari potest? Pro argumento hæc non adduxi, sed vt monerem tantum, quid olim pepererit mali Ecclesiæ ista excommunicatio. Sic autem probaui. Constat ab omnibus fermè olim fuisse creditum, poenam grauissimam esse Sacramentorum negationem, adeo vt plerique de salute illorum ambigerent, qui absque eis ex hac vita migrassent. An exciderunt tibi Augustini hac de re habitæ disputationes; vt alios taceam? Certe non audebis dicere, opinor, eos plus Baptismo quam cœnæ tribuisse. Propter hanc opinionem, inquam, quæ tunc non idiotas solum, sed etiam doctos inuaserat, statutum fuit, vt in extremo aut magno vitæ discrimine constitutis cœna Dominica concederetur, etiamsi excommunicati essent, imò scriptum creditumque fuit, aliquos non potuisse mori, priusquam cœnæ participes facti fuissent. Quis dubitet, præter te, sic fuisse tunc homines ratiocinatos? Negatio cœnæ adfert interitum. Ergo eiusdem concessio adfert salutem. Interroga tuam ipsius conscientiam, an non verisimile & propè necessarium putes talem plurimorum fuisse tunc opinionem. Vtinam tu tua vel hoc modo probare potuisses, quomodo ego coniecturam hanc meam ostendi esse probabilem.
units.tr: You also carp at what I said: that the prohibition of the use of the sacraments crept into the Church either then, when people began to attribute salvation to them, or at least arose from that error. You ask for proof of this dream of mine, as you call it. I suppose you were dreaming it yourself. Does the matter not itself show that it needs no further proof? Consider it for a moment and you will agree. Have I not nevertheless proved it sufficiently, as far as such a matter can be proved? I did not offer these points as an argument; I only wished to warn what harm that excommunication once brought upon the Church. But I did prove it in this way. It is agreed by almost everyone that it was once believed that the greatest punishment is the denial of the sacraments, so much so that many doubted the salvation of those who departed this life without them. Have the disputations of Augustine on this matter slipped your mind, to say nothing of others? Surely, I think, you will not dare to say that they valued Baptism more highly than the Lord's Supper. Because of this opinion, I say, which then had taken hold not only of the unlearned but also of the learned, it was decreed that the Lord's Supper should be granted to those in extreme danger or in great peril of life, even if they were excommunicated. Indeed, it was written and believed that some could not die before they had become partakers of the Supper. Who, apart from you, would doubt that people reasoned in this way at that time? To deny the Supper brings ruin; therefore granting it brings salvation. Examine your own conscience and say whether you do not think that such an opinion held by many at that time is probable and almost necessary. I wish you could have proved your own points in this way, as I have shown my conjecture to be probable.

units.la: · Vltimo loco ponis hoc argumentum meum. E medio tollere, & Satanæ tradere (ad interitum carnis) idem significant. At ex Ecclesia eijcere & è medio tollere non significant idem. Ergo neque ex Ecclesia eijcere, & Satanæ tradere eadem sunt. Quippe cum è medio tolli malum iubet Apostolus, alludit ad dictum Mosis 13. Deuter. quo in loco pro occidere ponitur illud, è medio tollere. Sed cum Ecclesia tunc careret Magistratu, atq; idcirco gladio careret, precibus à Deo iubet impetrare, ut nefarium hominë interficeret. Sanè si nullo alio argumento refelli posset vestra excommunicatio, vel vnû hoc sufficere posset. Etenim Apostolus cum sceleratum vult puniri, non iubet eû excommunicari, nec adducit scripturæ testimoniû hoc iubentis: sed vult eû interfici: & scripturæ testimonio declarat recte hoc ita fieri ex voluntate atque ordinatione Dei. Quid tu? Respondeas quatuor adfers. Prima est, probauimus ex ijs scriptoribus, quorum authoritate abusus es, Satanæ tradere non esse interficere. Secunda, Nô scripsit simpliciter vt tolleretur è medio, quod significat mortis supplicium, sed addit pronomen ὑμῶν vestri. Aliud autem est, tolli è medio, quam tolli è medio Ecclesiæ Corinthiacæ. Tertia, Si idem sunt, tradere Satanæ, & è medio tollere, consequitur, ius tradendi Satanæ penès Corinthios fuisse, cum eos iubeat malum è medio sui tollere. Ad hæc primum respondebimus: deinde vltimam confutabimus.
units.tr: Last, you set out my argument: "to remove from the midst" and "to deliver to Satan" (for the destruction of the flesh) mean the same thing. But "to cast out of the Church" and "to remove from the midst" do not mean the same thing. Therefore neither are "to cast out of the Church" and "to deliver to Satan" the same. Indeed, when the Apostle orders that the evil be removed from the midst, he alludes to the saying of Moses in Deuteronomy 13, where in that passage "to remove from the midst" is used in place of "to kill". But since the Church then lacked the magistrate, and therefore lacked the sword, he orders them to obtain by prayers from God that he should slay the wicked man. Certainly, if your excommunication could be refuted by no other argument, this one alone would be sufficient. For when the Apostle wants a wicked man punished, he does not order him to be excommunicated, nor does he cite a text of Scripture commanding this; rather he wants him to be slain, and by the testimony of Scripture he declares that this is rightly done by the will and ordinance of God. What do you say? You offer four answers. The first is that we have proved, from those writers whose authority you have abused, that to deliver to Satan is not to kill. The second is that he did not write simply that he should be removed from the midst, which signifies the punishment of death, but added the pronoun "your" [ὑμῶν]. Yet to be removed from the midst is one thing, and to be removed from the midst of the Corinthian Church is another. The third is that if "to deliver to Satan" and "to remove from the midst" are the same, it follows that the right to deliver to Satan belonged to the Corinthians, since he orders them to remove the evil from among themselves. To these points we shall first reply; then we shall refute the last.

units.la: · Ad primam respondeo, falsum esse, te ex illis authoribus probauisse, quod dicis. Etenim Augustinus aperte loquitur de sublatione è medio. Quinetiam lib. 5. quæst. 39. in Deuter. tollere è medio palàm dicit significare interficere: idque probat 2. argumentis. Primum est, quod Apostol. testimonium ex Deuteron. desumpserit. Alterum est, quia dicat, τὸν ἀνθρωπον, non autem τὸ ἀνθρωπον. Athanasius ait exceptam fuisse ab Apostolo animam, quod verum est: at per animam non intellexit hanc vitam mortalem, vt tu perperam affirmas. De alijs nunc nihil dicam: sed hoc solum attingam, te rursum iniuria me afficere, cum me horum virorum authoritate scribis abusum esse. Quippe hoc solum volui ipsorum testimonijs probare, aliud ipsos existimasse Satanæ traditionem, quam Sacramentorum interdictionem: quod negare tu non potes: quantumuis non eodem plane modo exponant hunc locum.
units.tr: To the first I reply that it is false that you have proved from those authors what you say. For Augustine speaks plainly of removal from the midst. Moreover, in Book 5, Question 39 on Deuteronomy, he openly says that to remove from the midst means to kill, and he proves this by two arguments. The first is that the Apostle took the testimony from Deuteronomy. The second is that the text says "the man" [τὸν ἄνθρωπον], not "the thing" [τὸ ἄνθρωπον]. Athanasius says that the soul was excepted by the Apostle, which is true; but by soul he did not mean this mortal life, as you wrongly assert. I will say nothing now about the others, but I will touch on this alone: you again do me wrong when you write that I have abused the authority of these men. Indeed I wished to prove from their testimonies only this, that they thought the delivering to Satan to be something other than the prohibition of the sacraments. This you cannot deny, although they do not explain this passage in exactly the same way.

units.la: Ad secundam dico, pronomen ἐμῶν sententiæ nostræ neque addere neque detrahere. Cum enim iubet eos malum illum tollere è medio siue hominum & mundi, siue è medio sui vel Ecclesiæ, idem iubet. Si, quod tu dicis, sensisset, perinde id esset, ac si quis Virginis pudicitiam iuberet conseruare, & eandem imperaret ex honestarum matronarum cœtu in prostibulum siue Lupanar detrudi.
units.tr: To the second I say that the pronoun "your" [ἐμῶν, read as ὑμῶν] neither adds to nor takes away from our position. For when he orders them to remove that evil from the midst, whether of men and of the world, or of themselves or of the Church, he orders the same thing. If, as you say, he had meant that, it would be just as if someone ordered the chastity of a virgin to be kept, and at the same time commanded her to be thrust out from the company of respectable matrons into a brothel or a stew.

units.la: Ad tertiam respondeo, Corinthios habuisse potestatem incestuosum hominem è medio tollendi, quomodo Apostolus eos facere debuisse indicat, nempe vt luctu & precibus à Deo impetrarent, vt, quomodo ei visum fuisset, ita eum tolleret. Satanæ traderenon iubet, quæ potestas Apostoli fuit, non Corinthiorum, sed conuenire iubet, vt eis congregatis ipse eum spiritu presens traderet. E medio tollere, si Corinthios spectes, generalius erat: si Apostolum spectes, eadem erant, quo tempore hoc modo tollere decreuerat.
units.tr: To the third I reply that the Corinthians had the power to remove the incestuous man from the midst, just as the Apostle indicates they ought to do, namely by obtaining it from God with grief and prayers, so that he would remove him in whatever way seemed good to him. He does not order them to deliver him to Satan; that was the power of the Apostle, not of the Corinthians; but he orders them to assemble, so that he himself, present in spirit, might deliver him. To remove from the midst, if you look at the Corinthians, was more general; if you look at the Apostle, the two were the same, at the time when he had decided to remove him in this way.

units.la: In responsione quarta & vltima plus inest rei. Primum dicis non tantum cap. 13. Deuter. poni verba hæc, tollite malum è medio vestri, sed alibi sæpius: id quod verum est. Nam in meis Thesibus, quas postremò correxi, ostendi eadem verba, imò easdem pene syllabas contineri Deuteron. 17. & 19. & 21. & 22. ter, & tandem 24. cap. semel. In omnibus his locis positum est ἐξαίρειν siue ἐξαιρεῖς cum in cap. 13. pro eo posuisset ἐξαιρῆτε. Cum ergo dicis, si capitale supplicium ubique significet hæc phrasis causam nullam esse cur accusetur Draco, quasi leges sanguine scripserit: quum futurum sit, ut Moses multo magis sanguinarius inveniatur. Haec tu cum inusitatam hanc tuam audaciam confidero, qui Apostolum & Mosen, adeoque Deum ipsum, audes corrigere, non possum non exhorrescere: Impie audax sit, qui negare sciens velit, in omnibus citatis locis phrasim hanc significare capitalem poenam a Magistratu infligendam. Nec propterea vel Moses, vel Apostoli, vel Deus ipse recte a te vocabuntur sanguinarij.
units.tr: In the fourth and last answer there is more substance. First you say that these words, "remove the evil from among you", occur not only in Deuteronomy chapter 13 but more often elsewhere; and this is true. For in my Theses, which I last corrected, I showed that the same words, indeed nearly the same syllables, are found in Deuteronomy 17, 19, 21, and 22 three times, and finally once in chapter 24. In all these places the Greek is ἐξαίρειν or ἐξαιρεῖς, whereas in chapter 13 he had used ἐξαιρῆτε. Therefore when you say that if this phrase everywhere signifies capital punishment, there is no reason why Draco should be accused, as though he had written his laws in blood, it will follow that Moses is found to be far more bloodthirsty. When I consider this unusual audacity of yours, in that you dare to correct the Apostle and Moses, and God himself, I cannot help but shudder. Whoever knowingly wishes to deny that in all the places cited this phrase signifies capital punishment to be inflicted by the magistrate is impiously bold. Nor, for that reason, will Moses, or the Apostles, or God himself be rightly called bloodthirsty by you.

units.la: At sani interpretes, ais, monent, interdum ista esse referenda ad ipsius Dei iudicium. Non hoc quaerimus, an aliquando Deus interminetur aliquibus etiam familijs exitium, sed ser in his locis, ex quibus verba sua constat Apostolum sumpsisse, id voluerit? Cum de se-ipso loquitur Deus, non dicit scriptura, aufer hunc, vel auferte hunc e medio vestri: sed dicit, excindetur, succidetur, peribit, alijque similibus vtitur loquendi formulis.
units.tr: But, you say, sound interpreters warn that these things are sometimes to be referred to God's own judgment. We do not ask whether God at some time threatens destruction even upon some families; but in those places from which, as is clear, the Apostle took his words, did he mean that? When God speaks of himself, Scripture does not say "take this one away" or "take away this one from among you", but says "he shall be cut off", "he shall be hewn down", "he shall perish", and uses other similar forms of speech.

units.la: In citatis omnibus locis mandat Deus expresse per Mosen Magistratui, ut tales afficiat capitis supplicio. Non memini adhuc me in sacris libris hanc loquendi formam, [illegible, ~12 letters] positum reperisse pro eo, quod est, [illegible, ~10 letters]. Vides quousque procedas dum figmentum humanum vis hominibus venditare pro mandato Diuino?
units.tr: In all the places cited God expressly commands through Moses that the magistrate punish such persons with capital punishment. I do not recall, so far, having found in the sacred books this form of speech [illegible, about 12 letters] used in place of what is [illegible, about 10 letters]. Do you see how far you go when you want to pass off a human invention to men as a divine command?

units.la: Haec sunt, quae in expositione nostra huius loci Apostolici carpere & denigrare, sed infelicissimo conatu tentasti. Quippe non modo non maculasti ea, sed animi tui affectum praeclare nobis prodidisti, quantumuis fratris appellatione subinde tegere eum conatus sis.
units.tr: These are the points which you tried, with a most unhappy effort, to carp at and disparage in our exposition of this Apostolic passage. For you not only did not stain them, but you have clearly revealed to us the disposition of your mind, although you have tried from time to time to cover it with the name of brother.

units.la: Prudentius fecisse aliquibus videris, quod libenter quaedam praeterieris. Tale est argumentum a verbo [illegible, ~8 letters] deductum hoc modo. Vbicunque verbum hoc sic est positum in sacris literis, quomodo hic a Paulo positum cernimus, semper significat potestati alicuius permittere ad hoc faciendum, cuius causa aliquis traditur. Con-
units.tr: You seem to have been prudent in some respects, since you gladly passed over certain points. The argument drawn from the word [illegible] goes like this. Wherever this word is used in Holy Scripture in the way we see Paul using it here, it always means to hand someone over to the power of another, for whose sake the person is delivered up.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] struitur autem in hoc loco sic, vt Nominatiuus personæ tradentis præcedat, sequatur Accusatiuus personæ traditæ, vnà cum Datiuo personæ, cui traditur, ac tandem id, cuius causa, & quatenus traditur. Talis ergo est oratio, ac si dicerem: tradidi filium meum præceptori ad castigationem. Ita cum dico, an non hoc dico, potestatem me præceptori dedisse castigandi filium? Dicam aliquid amplius: nec apud sacros scriptores nec apud profanos verbum hoc reperies vnquam sic positum, quin idem significet ac permittere, in potestatem dare vel dedere. Exempla sunt in 1. ad Timoth. 1. Actor. 27. & 28. Matth. 5. 18. 27. Marc. 15. Ioh. 19. Simillimum est, quod Matth. 24. habetur, παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς θλῖψιν: & Marc. 15. παραδοθήσεται δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον. Item 2. Pet. 2. παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. Item 2. cap. Iobi, ἐπὶ παραδέδωκά σοι αὐτόν: μόνον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ φυλάξαι. Hoc tu argu-mentum dissoluere debuisses: atque alia quaedam ad rem non adeo pertinentia omittere.
units.tr: It is constructed in this passage so that the nominative of the person delivering comes first, followed by the accusative of the person delivered, together with the dative of the person to whom he is delivered, and finally the matter for which, and the extent to which, he is delivered. The sentence is therefore like saying: "I handed my son over to a teacher for correction." When I say this, do I not mean that I gave the teacher power to chastise my son? I will say more: you will never find this word used in this way in sacred or profane writers without it meaning the same as to permit, or to give or deliver into someone's power. Examples are in 1 Timothy 1; Acts 27 and 28; Matthew 5:18, 27; Mark 15; John 19. Most similar is what is found in Matthew 24: they will deliver you up to tribulation [παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς θλῖψιν]; and in Mark 15: brother will deliver up brother to death [παραδοθήσεται δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον]. Likewise 2 Peter 2: they will bring in destructive heresies [παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας]. Likewise Job 2: behold, I have delivered him into your hand; only spare his life [ἐπὶ παραδέδωκά σοι αὐτόν: μόνον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ φυλάξαι]. You ought to have refuted this argument, and to have left out certain other matters that do not bear on the point.

units.la: Ne ad hoc quidem respondes, quod dixi, nullo authore idoneo monstrari posse ἐξάρτωτ ἐκ μέσου ποιῆσαι, idem esse aut significare, quod arcere à Sacramentis, vel excommunicare. Nam si pro eijcere maximè alicubi positum esset hoc verbum, hic non posset tamen ita accipi. Cum enim dicat, ἐκ μέσῳ ὑμῶν ad Gentiles fuisset exturbandus. At obstat quod dicit, vt anima salua sit, quae extra consortium Ecclesiae salua esse nequit. Si à solo Sacramentorum vsu priuatoque commercio duntaxat arcuissent, nondum è medio sui sustulissent. Si ad refipiscentiam vsque eijciendum fuisse ad Gentiles dicas, scriptum hoc nullibi esse, sed à te verbis Apostoli assui constanter verèq; respondeo. Non enim huius rei meminit Apostolus vnica syllaba: imò nec vllius receptionis commeminit, dum eum tradi velle scribit. Ac post intercessionem Corinthiorum, quando culpam ei condonat, non iubet recipi ad Sacramenta, sed sufficere ait ἐπιτιμίαν, maioreque eum poena non vult affici.
units.tr: Nor do you answer what I said: that no trustworthy author can be shown to use to take out of the midst [ἐξάρτωτ ἐκ μέσου ποιῆσαι] as meaning, or as equivalent to, to keep away from the sacraments or to excommunicate. For even if this verb were most often used elsewhere in the sense of to cast out, it could not be taken so here. For when he says out of the midst of you [ἐκ μέσῳ ὑμῶν], it would have to mean that they were to be driven out among the Gentiles. But there is the objection that he adds, that the spirit may be saved, whereas one who is outside the fellowship of the Church cannot be saved. If they had only been kept from the use of the sacraments and from private intercourse, they would not yet have been removed from their midst. If you say that he must be cast out to the Gentiles until repentance, I reply that this is written nowhere, but is something you have constantly and falsely added to the words of the Apostle. For the Apostle does not mention this matter by a single syllable; indeed he does not mention any readmission at all, while he writes that he wishes him to be delivered up. And after the intercession of the Corinthians, when he forgives him the fault, he does not order him to be received back to the sacraments, but says that the rebuke [ἐπιτιμίαν] is sufficient, and does not wish him to be punished more severely.

units.la: Item locum te oportebat osteudere, in quo Apostolus iusserit vel Presbyteris vel alijs vllis quempiam Satanæ tradere ad interitum carnis. Scribit vbique se cum authoritate venturum: se asperum fore & rigidum: se pro potestate à Deo, Sibi, non Ecclesiæ, non alijs, concessa acturum: se cum virga venturum: peccantesque imperat per Epistolam, Sibi, indicari, non iubet à Presbyteris excommunicari aut Satanæ dedi. Erat hoc Apostolicæ authoritatis, quibus non sanandi modo, verumetiam percutiendi facultatem Deus concesserat. Nullos quoque ordinauisse eum legimus Presbyteros, qui hoc munus in Ecclesia gererent. Timotheum iubet quidem peccantes coràm omnibus siue palàm arguere: Satanæ tradere siue excommunicare aliquem neque hunc neque alium quempiam iubet. Illustre argumentum hoc quoque facit, quod 1. Timoth. 1.de Hymenaeo & Alexandro loquens scribit, se (non Ecclesiam, non Presbyteros, non alios quosuis) eos Satanæ tradidisse. Quibus permotus videtur Petrus Martyr, vt in 6.cap. Comm.in lib. Iudicum scripserit, his verbis: Paulus & cæteri Apostoli Cacodæmones habuere sibi subiectos: & per eos nonnunquam eis licuit fontes ad salutem suam punire. Iccirco quibus huiusmodi donum concessum non est, ijab eo exercendo abstinere debent. Quantò rectius hic author, qui tamen vestræ disciplinæ hostis non fuit, quam tu de hoc Apostoli facto iudicarit, ex bis satis liquet.
units.tr: You also ought to have pointed out the place where the Apostle ordered either the elders or any others to deliver someone to Satan for the destruction of the flesh. Everywhere he writes that he will come with authority: that he will be severe and stern: that he will act by the power given him by God, to himself, not to the Church, not to others: that he will come with a rod. And when he commands by letter that sinners be dealt with, he orders that they be pointed out to himself; he does not order them to be excommunicated by the elders or given over to Satan. This was the authority of an apostle, to whom God had granted the power not only of healing but also of striking. We also read that he appointed no elders to carry out this office in the Church. He does indeed bid Timothy to rebuke sinners openly before all; but he does not order him, or anyone else, to deliver anyone to Satan or to excommunicate. He also makes a striking argument in 1 Timothy 1, where, speaking of Hymenaeus and Alexander, he writes that he (not the Church, not the elders, not any others whatever) had delivered them to Satan. Moved by this, Peter Martyr seems to have written, in his commentary on the sixth chapter of the Book of Judges, in these words: "Paul and the other Apostles had demons subject to them, and through them it was sometimes permitted to them to punish those who were to be saved. Therefore those to whom such a gift has not been granted ought to abstain from exercising it." How much more correctly this author judged the Apostle's act than you have done, although he was no enemy of your discipline, is clear enough from these things.

units.la: Item cum in 1. Cap. poster. Epistol. ait, eos sic tristatos fuisse secundum Deum, vt damnum seu detrimentum abeo nullum acceperint, satis docet, quid futurum fuisset, si non tanto studio pro eo comprecati fuissent. Etenim suo moerore & precibus veniam illi misero impetrauerunt: quod nisi factum fuisset damnum fuissent perpesi, nempe amisissent illum. Sanè pro detrimento non potuissent iudicare, si ad poenitentiæ solum prouocationem fuisset à Sacramentis reiectus. Lucrum potius futurum fuerat, proque eo multis tis modis gaudendum ipsis fuisset. Dicitis enim ad lu-crandum peccatores Excommunicationem instituta esse.
units.tr: Again, when in the first chapter of the second epistle he says that they were grieved in a godly way, so that they suffered no loss or harm from him, he sufficiently shows what would have happened had they not prayed for him with such zeal. For by their sorrow and prayers they obtained pardon for that wretched man; and unless this had been done they would have suffered loss, namely they would have lost him. Certainly they could not have judged it a loss if he had been cast out from the sacraments only to provoke repentance. It would rather have been a gain, and they would have had many reasons for rejoicing over it. For you say that excommunication was instituted to gain sinners.

units.la: Haec & his similia solide refutare debebas, si tam candide ac strenue causam tuam agere decreueras. Sed vel vnicum argumentum illud nostrum, à verbo tradendi desumptum, omnes conatus vestros irritos faciat. Nec possum non extremè mirari, quod dicas tam confidenter, me in tota Scriptura ne vnum quidem apicem reperire, exquo confirmem tradere Satanæ, idem declarare, atque per Satanam interficere. Cur non tot argumenta, quæ sine causa nullaque cum ratione allatrasti, refutasti? Cur non ostendisti alicubi in scriptura verbum ταραδιδόναι hoc modo positum, vt hic est positum, aliud significare, quàm dedere, concedere, seu potestati alicuius permittere? Sed de hac re nimis multa dixi: tempus iam est, vt ad partem alteram, videlicet ad interpretationem tuam huius loci Apostolici deueniamus: & per lepida tua argumenta examinemus.
units.tr: You ought to have refuted these points and others like them solidly, if you had decided to plead your cause so frankly and vigorously. But that one argument of ours, taken from the word for delivering up, alone makes all your efforts vain. Nor can I help being greatly astonished that you so confidently say that I can find not even one iota in the whole of Scripture by which I may confirm that to deliver to Satan means the same as to destroy through Satan. Why did you not refute the many arguments which you have barked out without cause and without any reason? Why did you not show somewhere in Scripture that the verb to deliver up [παραδιδόναι], used in the way it is used here, means anything other than to give over, to grant, or to permit to someone's power? But I have said too much on this matter: it is now time that we turn to the other part, namely your interpretation of this apostolic passage, and examine it by means of your witty arguments.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CHAP. V.

units.la: Confutatio Argumentorum pro Excommunicatione ex loco Pauli 1. ad Corinth. cap. 5. exstructorum.
units.tr: Refutation of the arguments for excommunication built on Paul's passage in 1 Corinthians 5.

units.la: REgnum Satanæ, inquis, est Mundus. Ergo qui traditur Satanæ, ab Ecclesia iubetur exulare. Vehementer miror, si seriò istadicis de præsente loco? Quo argumento probabis Apostolum hic voluisse, per tradere Satanæ, intelligere, eijcere in mundum? An in Regno mundi seu Satanæ servantur animæ? At Apostolus hunc sic statuerat tradere Satanæ, vt salua maneret eius anima. Admiratione certè dignissimum est, vos tam anxiè solicitos esse, vt authoritatem habere videamini ex Christi membris membra Satanae efficiendi, cum contrarium potius studere conueniat, qua ratione scilicet non solum in Ecclesia agentes in eadem retineamus, verumetiam extra eam viuentes modis omnibus in ipsam pertrahamus, Luc. 14. At non ob aliud, inquies, prauos eiecimus, quam vt resipiscentes recipiamus: & ne membra putria totum corpus inficiant. Quasi verò facilius sit eiectos ad obedientiam reuocare, quam intra Ecclesiam permanentes sanare: ac desint Magistratui rationes iustae & legitimae, quibus quantumlibet pertinaces ad officium & honestam vitam cogat.
units.tr: You say that the kingdom of Satan is the world, and therefore whoever is delivered to Satan is ordered by the Church to be exiled. I am greatly surprised that you are serious in saying these things about the present passage. By what argument will you prove that the Apostle here meant by "to deliver to Satan" to cast out into the world? Are souls preserved in the kingdom of the world or of Satan? Yet the Apostle had decided to deliver this man to Satan in such a way that his soul would remain safe. It is truly most remarkable that you are so anxiously concerned to seem to have authority to make members of Satan out of members of Christ, when it would rather be fitting to strive for the opposite. By that reasoning, we would keep within the Church those who are in it, and by every means draw into it those who live outside it (Luke 14). But, you will say, we have cast out the wicked for no other reason than to receive them back when they repent, and so that the rotten members do not infect the whole body. As if it were easier to recall the expelled to obedience than to heal those who remain within the Church! As if the magistrate lacked just and lawful reasons by which he could compel even the most stubborn to duty and an honest life.

units.la: An non absurdè fecerit pater, si petulantem impudentemque virginem ex aedibus eijciat, vt meliorem redditam recipiat, dum domi suae rectius & commodius fraenare possit immoderatos affectus? Absurdius multò fecerit, qui non tantum ex aedibus ad alios, vbi tamen liberior sit futura eiciat, sed in Lupanari cum impurissimis scortis collocet, vt in illa societate castitatem & pudicitiam discat. Haud leuius peccatis vos, dum peccatores, quos intra Ecclesiam corrigere licet, extra eam expellitis. Quae res etsi est absurda, longè tamen absurdius est hoc, quòd non modo ex Ecclesia simpliciter extrudere vultis, verumetiam Satanae dedere, inque mundum, qui Satanae regnum est, intrudere conamini. Quid porrò Mundus, quoad Satan in eo regnat, aliud est, quàm regnum improbitatis, nequitiae, libidinis, immunditiae, impietatis? In hoc regnum qui aliquem ideo exturbat ex Ecclesia, vt melior efficiatur, an non perinde facit, atque is, qui Virginem lasciuam inter petulcas & prostitutae libidinis foeminas viuere cogat, quò castior facta eam ad pudentes & verecundas reuocet? An non facilius inter filios Dei, quam inter Satanae mancipia sanabuntur peccatores? Hanc viam corrigendi improbos non praescripsit populo suo Deus in Veteri foedere, sed intra Ecclesiam ad obedientiam cogi mandauit.
units.tr: Would not a father act absurdly if he threw a wanton and shameless daughter out of his house, so that she might be received back improved, when at home he could more properly and conveniently restrain her immoderate passions? Far more absurdly would he act who not only threw her out of the house to others, where she would be freer, but placed her in a brothel among the most impure harlots, so that she might learn chastity and modesty in that company. You sin no less when you expel from the Church sinners whom it is lawful to correct within it. Although this is absurd, it is far more absurd that you are not content simply to thrust them out of the Church, but also try to deliver them to Satan and to push them into the world, which is the kingdom of Satan. Moreover, what is the world, insofar as Satan reigns in it, other than a kingdom of wickedness, lust, uncleanness and impiety? Does not the one who drives someone out of the Church into this kingdom, in order that he may become better, do just the same as one who forces a wanton virgin to live among shameless women and harlots, so that, having become more chaste, she may be called back to modest and decent company? Will sinners not be healed more easily among the sons of God than among the slaves of Satan? God did not prescribe this way of correcting the wicked to his people in the Old Covenant; he commanded that they be compelled to obedience within the Church.

units.la: Haud recte quoque simlilitudo putridi membri adferturr:
units.tr: Nor is the likeness of a rotten limb rightly brought forward.

units.la: Primum quidem, quoniam similitudines nihil probant, quoties praeceptum Dei non exstat. Deinde verò etiam, quoniam non congruit instituto. Quippe nulli omninò peccatores, nedum illi, de quibus nos adhuc egimus, (Excipi semper volo pertinaces haereticos in fundamento salutis errantes, & in Spiritum-sanctum peccantes) sic sunt, dum viuunt, desperati, quomodò putre & emortuum membrum insanabile est. Imò sicut putrescens membrum, nondum tamen mortuum, sanabile est, quantisper corpori cōtinuatum coliaeret, insanabile autem, cum primum resectum à corpore fuerit, redditur, ita ferè sanabiles sunt peccatores in Ecclesia retenti potius, quam expulsi. Praeterea non est necesse sic alios à malis contaminari, quomodò membra sana necessarium est à putridis corrumpi. Nam vt lignum non potest non comburi ab igne tangente, sic non possunt non membra inter se continuata à se mutuo pati, cum homines ratione vtentes cauere sibi possint. Postremò non potest ab hominibus aliquis in mundum, quatenus is est regnum Satanae, ex Ecclesia eijci, sed ex visibili tantum Ecclesia expelli potest. At hic, si modò fidem retinet, quantumuis sepulta aliquandiu iacuerit, non est in mundo, regno videlicet Satanae, sed in Ecclesia, licet inter medios Turcas viuere cogatur. Qui autem fidem non retinet, in mundo est, etiamsi inter visibilis Ecclesiae membra nobilissimum atque optimum iudicetur esse. Sanè ex Ecclesia in mundum eijcere, nil est aliud quā damnationis sententiam exsequi, quod hominibus nequaquam competit. Proinde non recte à te dicitur Apostolus Corinthium iussisse aut voluisse in mundū, Satanae regnū, expellere, cum animam voluerit saluam manere in die Domini: quae in mundo hoc salua manere non potuit. Nihil igitur aliud facitis Excommunicando, quam quod vel adigitis infirmos & rudes ad desperationem, vel efficitis insignes & magnos Hypocritas, quos peccatoribus alijs grauius odit Dominus. Deinde non vides te principium petere, & pro certo probatoque sumere, cuius probationem à te praecipuè flagitamus? Satanae tradere negamus idem esse, quod extra Ecclesiam eijcere, imò probamus eadem esse non posse. Haec cum tu refutare non potueris, quomodo sine pudore veluti confessum nihilominus sumere ausus es? Aliud est, cum scriptura dicit, Paulus juxta potestatem à Deo sibi concessam, tradidit hunc nefarium Satanę ad interitum corporis, vt nihilominus salua maneret anima: & aliud rursus, cum dico: hic traditus est Satanae in suum regnum: seu traditus est in Mundum. Argumenta nostra semper manent integra. Paulus iubet eum ἐξαρειῶσθαι ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν : at hoc non est in mundum eijcere. Paulus vult eum Satanae tradi τῷ ὀλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς: at hoc non est in mundum proijci. Omitto iam cætera, quae ex superioribus & Thessalonicensibus nostris peti poterunt.
units.tr: First, because comparisons prove nothing whenever no command of God exists. Second, because it does not fit the matter at hand. Indeed no sinners at all, much less those of whom we have been speaking (I always want to except stubborn heretics who err concerning the foundation of salvation, and those who sin against the Holy Spirit), are, while they live, desperate in the way that a rotten and dead limb is incurable. Rather, just as a rotting limb that is not yet dead can be healed as long as it still clings to the body, but becomes incurable as soon as it has been cut off from the body, so sinners who are retained in the Church rather than expelled are for the most part curable. Moreover, it is not necessary that others be contaminated by evils in the way that sound limbs must be corrupted by rotten ones. For just as wood touched by fire cannot help burning, so limbs joined together cannot help suffering from one another, whereas men who use reason can take care of themselves. Lastly, no one can be cast out of the Church by men into the world, insofar as the world is the kingdom of Satan; a man can be expelled only from the visible Church. But this man, if he still retains faith, though he may lie buried for a time, is not in the world, that is, in the kingdom of Satan, but in the Church, even if he is forced to live among the Turks. He who does not retain faith is in the world, even if he is judged the noblest and best of the members of the visible Church. Certainly to cast someone out of the Church into the world is nothing other than to carry out a sentence of damnation, which in no way belongs to men. Therefore you are wrong to say that the Apostle ordered or wished the Corinthian to be expelled into the world, the kingdom of Satan, when he wished the soul to remain safe in the day of the Lord; a soul could not remain safe in the world. Therefore, by excommunicating you do nothing else than either drive the weak and simple to despair, or make notorious and great hypocrites, whom the Lord hates more than other sinners. Furthermore, do you not see that you beg the question, and take as certain and proved what we most of all demand you prove? We deny that to deliver to Satan is the same as to cast out of the Church; indeed we prove that they cannot be the same. Since you have not been able to refute this, how have you shamelessly dared to assume it anyway, as if it were conceded? It is one thing when Scripture says, "Paul, according to the power given him by God, delivered this wicked man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his soul might nonetheless remain safe"; and it is another when I say, "here he has been delivered to Satan into his kingdom," or "he has been delivered into the world." Our arguments always remain intact. Paul commands that he be taken away from among them [ἐξαρειῶσθαι ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν]; but this is not to cast out into the world. Paul wishes him to be delivered to Satan for the destruction of the flesh [τῷ ὀλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς]; but this is not to be thrown out into the world. I now pass over the rest, which can be sought from what has been said above and from our remarks on the Thessalonians.

units.la: Argumentum alterum tuum est, Paulum de spiritualibus locutum esse: ac proinde non interpretanda haec de poena corporali aut politica. Quasi vero Petrus non egerit de spiritualibus, cum corporaliter Ananiam occidit: aut Paulus de corporalibus rebus disputarit, cum Elymam Magum excoecauit: aliquos Satanae tradidit: & hunc ad interitum carnis tradere apud se statuit. An τῷ ὀλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς, & nostra mors temporaria spiritualis est, atque ad corpus non pertinet, cum propter peccata eam patimur? Quo medio probabis, corporali poena seu politica nunquam vel Deum vel Apostolos peccata puniuisse?
units.tr: Your second argument is that Paul spoke of spiritual matters, and therefore these words must not be interpreted of corporal or civil punishment. As if Peter had not spoken of spiritual matters when he struck Ananias dead bodily, or Paul had not dealt with bodily things when he blinded Elymas the magician, and delivered certain people to Satan, and decided to deliver this man to the destruction of the flesh! Or is our temporal death spiritual and not pertaining to the body, when we suffer it because of sins? By what means will you prove that God or the Apostles never punished sins with a bodily or civil penalty?

units.la: Tertium est, Si factum tale quid fuisset ab Ecclesia, permagna fuisset calumniantibus parata probatio, voluisse cos ius sibi vsurpare Magistratuum. Multò maior parata pijs nunc est vestrum commentum refellendi occasio, cum vobis, quanquam estis subditi, Magistratus subiicitis. Sed, rogo te, an non contendimus Ecclesiis hoc non licere, sed potestatem hanc fuisse solis Apostolis concessam? An ideo calumniantibus praebita fuit occasio maledicendi, quia Ananiam cum uxore interfecit Petrus? & quia Magum excoecauit Paulus? Et alios quosdam Satanae absolute tradidit? Aliter loquitur Scriptura.
units.tr: Your third argument is that if such a thing had been done by the Church, the slanderers would have had a very great proof ready, namely that they wished to usurp the right of the magistrates. Now a much greater opportunity for the godly to refute your invention is ready, since, although you are subjects, you subject yourselves to the magistrates. But I ask you: do we not contend that this is not permitted to the Churches, and that this power was granted to the Apostles alone? Was an occasion for slanderers to speak evil given because Peter killed Ananias with his wife? Or because Paul blinded the magician? Or because he absolutely delivered certain others to Satan? Scripture speaks otherwise.

units.la: Quartum est, Si Christiani Magistratus tollerent omnes ebriosos, scortatores, & similes, gladio, multis carnificum millibus esset opus: & desinerent homines peccare potius poenae formidine, quàm virtutis amore. Non dixi ego omnes quomodocunque peccantes capitali supplicio plectendos esse: sed illos, quos vel lex Divina, vel Cesarum edicta ita damnant. Reliqui pro circumstantia locorum & temporum castigari poterunt. Satis Deo factum est, cum scelera quacunq; ratione honesta cohibentur & coherCentur, etiamsi vna eademque poena non semper & vbique puniantur. Hoc certum est, Deum velle, vt, quae iussit ac voluit olim à Magistratu puniri, hodie quoque ab eodem puniantur: etiamsi poenae formam non mandarit eandem vbique seruari. Non enim propter commenta nostra mutantur Dei consilia. Pharisaei eodem prope modo, quo vos hodie facitis, quaedam falsè in lege exponebant, quę Christus 15.cap. Matth. aperte damnat. Sed òro te, an facit malè, qui hac in parte facit, quod Deus iussit? Moses quantam multitudinem occidit Exod.32. Num.25? An Dauid peccauit, cum omne nefas sustulit, & Israelitas omnes Deo seruire coegit? An impiè Rex Asa fecit, qui interficiendos omnes statuit, non quaerentes Deum, 2.Paralip.15. Quam esses dignus, qui hoc loco aliam acciperes responsionem? Sed condonabo hoc Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Fourth, if Christian magistrates were to put to death with the sword all drunkards, fornicators and the like, there would be need of many thousands of executioners, and men would cease to sin from fear of punishment rather than from love of virtue. I did not say that all who sin in whatever way are to be punished with capital punishment, but those whom either the divine law or the edicts of Caesars condemn in this way. The rest may be chastised according to the circumstances of places and times. God is sufficiently satisfied when crimes are restrained and checked by any honest means, even if the same single penalty is not always and everywhere inflicted. This is certain: God wishes that what he once commanded and willed to be punished by the magistrate should be punished by the same today as well, even if he has not commanded that the same form of penalty be observed everywhere. For God's counsels are not changed because of our inventions. The Pharisees, in much the same way as you do today, explained some things in the law falsely, which Christ plainly condemns in Matthew 15. But I ask you, does he do wrong who in this matter does what God commanded? How many did Moses kill (Exodus 32; Numbers 25)? Did David sin when he removed every wickedness and compelled all Israelites to serve God? Did King Asa act impiously when he decided that all who did not seek God should be put to death (2 Chronicles 15)? How worthy you would be of receiving some other answer here! But I will overlook this for the Church.

units.la: Cur etiam nobis hic velut enorem & peccatum exprobas, quod Magistratum dicimus poenis prohibere scelera debere, & ad honeste viuendum earum formidine cogere? An non mandauit ei hoc Deus? Tollite hunc, inquit soepius, & obruite lapidibus, alitérue occidite, vt Israel videat actineat, tantumque facinus porrò, patrare nullus audeat. Te potius obiurgares, quod publicè non veritus es scribere ob id maximè vrgendam Excommunicationem vestram, quod si bonos non faciat, saltem hypocritas reddat. Tu modo non licitol.ypocritas facere studes, & me accusas, qui nil aliud doceo, quàm quod Deus mandauit. Moneo igitur te, vt cogites, quam hic mihi immanitatis iniuriam inurere voluisti, in Deum ipsum redundare, cuius doctrinam hic vrgeo. Deinde etiam, vt, quàm bellè solitus sis argumentari, notes. Multis opus foret Magistratui carnificibus, si malos punire omnes vellet: Ergo Apostolus per, tradere Satanae, intellexit Excommunicare.
units.tr: Why do you also reproach us here, as if it were an outrage and a sin, that we say the magistrate ought to restrain crimes by punishment and compel men to live honestly through fear of it? Did not God command him to do this? "Take him away," he often says, "and stone him, or kill him some other way, so that Israel may see and be afraid, and no one may dare to commit such a crime again." You should rather rebuke yourself, for you were not ashamed to write publicly that excommunication must be urged above all for this reason: that if it does not make men good, at least it makes them hypocrites. You are eager to make hypocrites, and yet you accuse me, who teach nothing but what God commanded. I advise you, therefore, to consider that the charge of cruelty you wished to fix upon me here recoils upon God himself, whose doctrine I am urging. Next, notice also how finely you are accustomed to argue. The magistrate would need many executioners if he wished to punish all the wicked. Therefore the Apostle, by "to deliver to Satan," understood excommunication.

units.la: Quintum est, Caro saepè significat carnis corruptionem: & opponitur spiritui seu regenerato homini. Ergo Paulus hic per carnis interitum intellexit carnis corruptionem seu prauitatem. Concedimus antecedens: at pernegamus & consequens & consequentiam. Nam nec sequitur consequens ex eo, quod antecedit: nec verum est: Nam carnis interitus hoc in loco, opponitur salutì animae, non caro spiritui: ac significat non exstinctionem affectuum malorum, sed mortem corporalem, vt efficacissimè supra probaui. Proba tu alicubi τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τῆς σαρκὸς pro morte seu restinctione prauitatis carnis nostrae poni. Aliud est caro, & aliud carnis interitus, vt hoc loco loquitur Apostolus. Longè aliud est, de quo ad Rom. loquitur, & de quo hic praecipit. Mirum est, te audere ista tam confidenter pro argumentis adferre, cum haec ipsa probanda tibi esse non nescias.
units.tr: Fifthly, flesh often signifies the corruption of the flesh, and it is opposed to the spirit or to the regenerate man. Therefore Paul, by the destruction of the flesh, understood the corruption or depravity of the flesh. We grant the antecedent, but we flatly deny both the consequent and the consequence. The consequent does not follow from what precedes it, nor is it true: for the destruction of the flesh in this place is opposed to the salvation of the soul, not flesh to spirit; and it signifies not the extinction of evil affections but bodily death, as I proved most effectively above. Prove somewhere that "the sin of the flesh" [τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τῆς σαρκὸς] is put for the death or extinction of the depravity of our flesh. Flesh is one thing, and the destruction of the flesh is another, as the Apostle speaks in this place. What he speaks of in the Epistle to the Romans, and what he here enjoins, are quite different. It is remarkable that you dare to bring these things forward so confidently as arguments, when you are not unaware that these very points need proof.

units.la: Responsum eodem modo fit ad sextum argumentum: quod cum quinto vel est idem, vel idem valet.
units.tr: The answer to the sixth argument is given in the same way, since it is either the same as the fifth or has the same force.

units.la: Septimum est, A carnifice Satana qui perimendus est, vel statim resipiscit, & nullo iure ab Ecclesia tradi potest, vt spiritus saluetur, qui iam saluus est: vel non resipiscit, & sic non erit saluus in die Domini. Nullus serpens percussus ita se toquet ac flectit, vt tu te-ipsum inflectis, vt aliquid inuenias. Non dicimus Apostolum voluisse Corinthium tradere Satanae ad interficiendum, vt hac conditione saluus fieret spiritus eius: sed voluisse enorme illud scelus morte punire, (vt Magistratus talia punire iussus est à Deo, vbi is est) quò terrorem alijs incuteret, eosque ab improbitate abstreret, ac ad pietatem reuocaret. Cuius rei coniecturam illud etiam probet, quod non simpliciter dicit, vt anima eius salua fit, sed addit in die Domini: quomodò de mortuis loqui solemus. Equidem Apostolus optimè de eo sperauit. uit, vt supra exposui: ideoque non dicit, se id facere vt seruetur spiritus ipsius, sed vt saluus sit in die Domini, sicut supra ex Chrysostomo tumet-ipse citafti. Terminū ergo hunc solum praescripsit Satanæ, quo non tentaret ac affligeret animum illius miseri, sed corpus solum necaret: quod Magistratus facere aliàs ex Dei mandato solet. Insipidae igitur nugae sunt tuae illae ratiunculae.
units.tr: The seventh argument is this: the executioner Satan, who is to be destroyed, either repents at once, and then by no right can he be handed over by the Church, so that the spirit may be saved, which is already saved; or he does not repent, and then he will not be saved on the day of the Lord. No serpent struck down twists and bends as you bend yourself in order to find something. We do not say that the Apostle wished the Corinthian to be handed over to Satan to be killed, so that on this condition his spirit might be saved. We say that he wished that enormous crime to be punished by death, as the magistrate is commanded by God to punish such crimes where he is in office, so as to strike terror into others and to turn them away from wickedness and call them back to godliness. The following also supports this conjecture: he does not simply say "that his soul may be saved," but adds "in the day of the Lord," as we are accustomed to speak of the dead. Indeed the Apostle hoped very well of him, as I set out above; and therefore he does not say that he does this so that his spirit may be preserved, but so that he may be saved in the day of the Lord, as you yourself cited from Chrysostom above. He therefore prescribed to Satan this limit only, so that Satan would not tempt and afflict the mind of that wretched man, but would destroy only the body, as the magistrate usually does by God's command. Your little reasonings are therefore insipid trifles.

units.la: Similis propemodum est octaua quoque ratio. An potest seruari alicuius anima, quæris, cuius corpus damnetur? Respondeo, si per damnationem corporis intelligas occisionem, affirmamus manifestius hoc esse, quàm vt idiota aliquis dubitare debeat, nedum tantus magister Israëlis. An enim non seruari animos eorum credis, quorum corpora à Magistratu vestro cremari iubentur, si piè moriantur? Vnde ergo hoc, quod quidam dixisse fertur, beatius mori istic homines, qui à carnifice occiduntur, quàm qui alibi domi suae moriuntur? Si de condemnatione æterna loqueris, nihil hoc ad nos pertinet, qui Apostolum scimus de morte corporis duntaxat locutum fuisse.
units.tr: The eighth argument is almost similar. You ask: can the soul of someone be saved whose body is condemned? I reply: if by the condemnation of the body you mean killing, we affirm this more plainly than any ignorant person ought to doubt, much less so great a teacher of Israel. For do you believe that the souls are not saved of those whose bodies your magistrate orders to be burned, if they die piously? Whence then comes that saying, reported to have been uttered by some, that men who are killed by the executioner there die more blessedly than those who die elsewhere at home? If you speak of eternal condemnation, this has nothing to do with us, who know that the Apostle spoke only of the death of the body.

units.la: Cum hisce coniungis tandem locum in 1. ad Timoth. 1. cap. de traditione Alexandri & Hymenaei &c. Ridiculum magis dici nihil potest, inquis, quàm occisum fuisse quempiam, vt sanctius de Deo sentire & loqui doceretur. Si voluisses fraternè interpretari nostra, non erat nobis hic opus defensione. Dixi enim Apostolum hos velut blasphemos & naufragos circa fidem Satanae tradidisse, sine illis conditionibus, quas in Corinthio notauit. Item videri mihi eos occisos fuisse à Satanae duabus de causis. Primum quidem, quod dicat se ipsi eos tradidisse (ἵνα παιδευθῶσι) vt edocti iam essent, non amplius blasphemare. Sermo hic vsitatus est satis apud nos, & talis fermè est, ac si Magistratus de fure Carnifici tradito dicat, se eum tradidisse, vt didicerit non furari amplius. Cum sic dicit, non hoc vult significare, cum à carnifice instituendum, vt non furetur, sed significat eum occidendum esse, vt non possit amplius furari. Sic Apostolus ait, fe eos Satanae interficiendos tradidisse, vt porrò amplius non possint blasphemare, sicut antea facere consueuerant. Deinde, quod ex Ecclesia eiecti non videntur cessaturi suisse à blasphemia. Etenim multò licentius tunc blasphemasent. Quid hic absurdi, alieni, & coacti reperitur?
units.tr: Finally you join with these arguments the passage in 1 Timothy 1 about the handing over of Alexander and Hymenaeus, and so on. "Nothing can be said," you say, "more ridiculous than that someone was killed so that he might be taught to think and speak more reverently of God." If you had wished to interpret our words in a brotherly way, there would have been no need for us to defend ourselves here. For I said that the Apostle delivered these men to Satan as blasphemers and shipwrecked in the faith, but without those conditions which I noted in the case of the Corinthian. Likewise, it seems to me that they were killed by Satan for two reasons. The first is that he says he delivered them "that they might be taught" [ἵνα παιδευθῶσι], so that they might already have been instructed no longer to blaspheme. This way of speaking is common enough among us, and it is much like a magistrate saying of a thief handed over to the executioner that he has handed him over so that he may have learned not to steal any more. When he speaks so, he does not mean that the man is to be instructed by the executioner not to steal; he means that the man is to be killed so that he can steal no more. So the Apostle says that he delivered them to Satan to be killed, so that they might no longer be able to blaspheme as they had been accustomed to do. The second reason is that, having been cast out of the Church, they did not seem likely to cease from blasphemy; for then they blasphemed far more freely. What here is absurd, foreign, or forced?

units.la: Principio dicis, verba subiunctiui modi talia, nonnunquam futuri quippiam denotare. Deinde praeteritum hic significare concedis, quoniam totum praeterierat. Addis deinde non me posse ex his verbis colligere euenisse, quod propositum erat Apostolo. Ego certè credo firmiter, Apostolum sic fuisse certum suae potestatis, vt, si quos ipsemet traderet Satanae occidendos, ij omninò ab eo occiderentur: praesertim verò mali, quales isti fuerunt, qui Apostolo multo tempore molesti exstiterant, & fidem abiecerant. Tibi liceat forte de Apostoli factis & dictis dubitare: mihi nec licet, nec vt liceat, volo. Tradidit ergo, vt non amplius possent blasphemare. Frustra igitur aceruas nugas, vt elabaris. At, inquis, Apostolus non dixit, vt non possint blasphemare, sed vt edocti sint non blasphemare. Concedo totum hoc: sed dico eum sic vsitatè fuisse locutū, quomodò etiam hodie de talibus rebus vulgò loquimur. Significatur enim hac oratione sic esse quempiam tractatum, vt poenam scelere suo dignam acceperit: & porrò scelestus esse nequeat.
units.tr: First you say that verbs in the subjunctive mood of this kind sometimes denote something future. Then you concede that the past is signified here, since the whole matter had already passed. You add that I cannot gather from these words that what the Apostle intended actually happened. I firmly believe, however, that the Apostle was so certain of his power that if he himself handed anyone over to Satan to be killed, those men were certainly killed by him; especially wicked men such as these, who had long troubled the Apostle and had cast off the faith. Perhaps you may be allowed to doubt the deeds and words of the Apostle; I am not allowed to, nor do I want to be. He therefore handed them over so that they could no longer blaspheme. In vain, then, do you heap up trifles in order to slip away. "But," you say, "the Apostle did not say that they might not be able to blaspheme, but that they might be taught not to blaspheme." I grant all this; but I say that he spoke in the customary manner, just as we commonly speak of such things even today. For this phrase signifies that someone has been dealt with in such a way that he has received a punishment worthy of his crime, and can no longer be wicked.

units.la: Quae postea de diuersitate horum & Corinthij addis, ad causam nostram non pertinent. Hoc sensi, Paulum de Corinthio optimè sperauisse: de alteris vtrum ita sperarit, nescire me fateor. Satanę non sentio eos ita ab Apostolo traditos, vt animas eorū vellet perdi. Hoc enim non est creaturae, sed solius Dei munus, seruare scilicet ac perdere animas. Poena igitur eos ad terrore aliorum affecit, vt Magistratus sceleratos afficere solet. Quod si repudiata impietate conuersi sunt ad Dominum, non obfuit mors corporalis saluti ipsorū. Vt dubitemus aliquo modo, id facit, quod & blasphemi fuerunt, & fidem abiecerunt. Porrò blasphemos iussisse Deum inter-fici fici Leuit. 24. nullus est, qui nesciat. Perfacile ex his intelligi poterit, frustra te hic Anathema obijcere, & comparationem inter hos & Corinthium facere. Merae sunt ambages, & putida sophismata: cum longissime aliud ego & dixerim & senserim.
units.tr: What you add afterwards about the difference between these men and the Corinthian does not pertain to our cause. I have held that Paul hoped well of the Corinthian; whether he hoped so of the others, I confess I do not know. I do not think that they were handed over to Satan by the Apostle in such a way that he wished their souls to perish. For to save or to destroy souls is not the office of a creature but the work of God alone. He therefore punished them to terrify others, as magistrates usually punish criminals. But if, having renounced their impiety, they turned to the Lord, bodily death did not harm their salvation. Lest we doubt in any way, he did this because they were both blasphemers and had cast off the faith. Moreover, that God commanded blasphemers to be put to death (Leviticus 24) no one is ignorant. From these things it will be very easy to understand that it is in vain for you to bring the anathema against us here, and to make a comparison between these men and the Corinthian. These are mere circumlocutions and rotten sophisms, since I have both said and thought something far different.

units.la: CAP. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: De Fermento.
units.tr: Concerning Leaven.

units.la: OFfem multa vere ac recte in tua interpretatione huius loci reprehendere & confutare: quae, ne a propósito nulla necessitate coactus discedam, in medio relinquam. Ergo largiar tibi, cum ita lubet, Apostolum ceremoniam prohibiti fermenti in celebratione Paschatis voluisse hic exponere: nec per similitudinem solum & allusionem argumentari, quod ego sentio. Quod inde commodi ad te redibit? Azymorum festum comparat Apostolus vitae nostrae toti, qua in hac viuimus peregrinatione, vt cum Iudaei ex Aegypto exibant, terram meliorem possessuri. Fermentum significat sceleratam vitam. Ex his sequitur, vt illis toto tempore festi illius non licuit fermentata edere: sic non licere nobis toto tempore vitae nostrae flagitiose agere. Quid ex his aliud sequitur, quam vt, quemadmodum fermentum edens interficiendus scribitur, ita etiam sceleratus interficiatur? Nihil horum contra nos facit. Sane qui fermentati aliquid edisset tota illa septimana, non iubetur a Paschate, (quod initium erat huius festi, sicut fides in Christum seu Spiritualis eius Christi pro nobis crucifixi principium est Christianae novaeque vitae) arceri, sed exterminari.
units.tr: I could rightly and truly reprove and refute many things in your interpretation of this passage, but lest I wander from the point without any necessity, I will set them aside. So I will grant you, since you wish it, that the Apostle here meant to explain the ceremony of the leaven forbidden in the celebration of the Passover, and that he does not argue only by likeness and allusion, as I hold. What advantage will come back to you from this? The Apostle compares the feast of unleavened bread to the whole of our life, which we live in this pilgrimage, just as the Jews, when they came out of Egypt, were about to possess a better land. Leaven signifies a wicked life. From this it follows that during the whole time of that feast it was not lawful to eat anything leavened; so it is not lawful for us to live wickedly during the whole time of our life. What else follows from this, than that just as the one who eats leaven is written to be put to death, so also the wicked man is to be put to death? None of this works against us. Indeed, one who had eaten anything leavened during that whole week was not ordered to be kept away from the Passover (which was the beginning of this feast, just as faith in Christ, or the spiritual reception of that Christ crucified for us, is the beginning of the Christian and new life), but to be cut off.

units.la: Non laboro etiam, verum Deum esse illum affirmes, qui exterminationem minetur ex populo Israelitico, an a Magistratu occidendum fuisse censeas. Prius magis consentaneum est alijs scripturae locis, similem modum loquendi habentibus, quos non est dubium de poena Diuina intelligendos esse. Videntur etiam huc facere, primum quidem historia, quod nullum legimus ob hanc causam occisum, licet multos legamus neglexisse: deinde quod Paulus in 11. cap. 1. ad Corinth. de indignè Coenam Domini edentibus scripsit. Certè septuaginta Interpretes verbum Hebraicum verbo Græco ἐξολοθρεύθησεται ubique Exodi scilicet 12. & 9. Num. interpretati sunt: quod nullo modo aliud potest, quam exstinctionem sive occisionem significare, à quocunque occidendus fuisse putetur.
units.tr: Nor do I trouble myself about whether you affirm that it was the true God who threatened exclusion from the people of Israel, or whether you think the offender ought to have been put to death by the magistrate. The former is more consistent with other passages of Scripture that have a similar way of speaking, which undoubtedly must be understood of divine punishment. The following also seem to favour this: first, the history, in that we read of no one killed for this cause, although we read that many neglected it; second, that Paul in 1 Corinthians 11 wrote of those who eat the Lord's Supper unworthily. Certainly the Seventy translators rendered the Hebrew verb everywhere (namely in Exodus 12 and Numbers 9) by the Greek word [ἐξολοθρεύθησεται]; this can in no way signify anything other than extinction or killing, by whomever the offender is thought to have been meant to be put to death.

units.la: Ergo videamus nunc, quomodo ex hisce, quae vltrò tibi largimur, propositum tuum argumenteris. Fermentum edentes arcebantur à Pascha te. At fermentum significavit scelera. Ergo scelerati sunt à nostris Sacramentis excludendi. Quam multa hic falsa sint, vide. Primum hoc falsum est, Deum scilicet alicui mandasse fermentum gustantem arcere à festo Azymorum, seu Paschatis. An idem significant hae duae orationes? Qui fermentata edet, exterminator: &, qui fermentata edit, à festi concelebratione arcetor. Tantundem certè differunt, quantum hæ duæ: Qui in concione ex pueris garriet, virgis caeditor: &, Pueri inter concionandum confabulantes excluduntur à concionibus: Sicut magister, cum pueris vetet confabulationes in templo sub certa poena, eos non emanere iubet, sic Deus, cum fermentum in festo Azymorum comedentibus interminetur excidium, non iubet à concelebratione festi excludi. Vterque praecipit facere, quod fieri debet: simulque poenam proponit non rite facientibus, quod facere iussi sunt.
units.tr: Let us see now how you argue your proposition from these things, which we grant you freely. Those who ate leaven were kept from the Passover. But leaven signified wickedness. Therefore wicked men are to be excluded from our sacraments. See how many things here are false. First, this is false: that God commanded that whoever tasted leaven be kept from the feast of unleavened bread, or the Passover. Do these two statements mean the same thing? "Whoever eats leavened bread shall be cut off," and "whoever eats leavened bread is kept from taking part in the celebration of the feast." They differ as much as these two: "Whoever chatters among the boys in the sermon is beaten with rods," and "Boys who chatter during the sermon are excluded from sermons." Just as a master, when he forbids conversation among the boys in the church under a fixed penalty, orders them not to go out, so God, when he threatens destruction to those who eat leaven at the feast of unleavened bread, does not order them to be excluded from taking part in the feast. Each commands that what ought to be done be done, and at the same time sets out a penalty for those who do not properly do what they were commanded to do.

units.la: Quod si maximè concederemus, Deum voluisse fermentum comedentes à festo Azymorum repelli, falsum nihilominus foret, eum propterea iussisse licentius improbiusque viuentes à Sacramentis nostris depellere. Etenim Azymorum festum, vt iam dictum est, non Coenam Dominicam, sed totum peregrinationis nostrae tempus significat. Quare non è Coena Domini, sed è vita excludendus erit scleratus. Longè differunt occisum seu exterminatum iri, & à Sacramentis depulsum, aut excommunicatum iri. Iam si istud etiam concederemus, excisionem, quam Deus interminatur fermentum comedentibus, significasse depulsionem à Sacramentis, falsum adhuc tamen permaneret hoc, nempe fermentata edentes ita figurauisse flagitiosos, ut vos vultis. Nam defendi Moses à contradictione manifesta non posset. Contradictoriae namque sunt hae duae enunciationes: omnes edant Pascha sub poena exitij sui, quicunque secundum legem mundi sunt: & aliqui secundum legem mundi, hoc est, qui peccatum aliquod admiserunt, non edant Pascha. Ex hisce satis apparet, quam sint infirma & lubrica, quae ex hac ceremonia extruitis pro vestrae excommunicationis defensione. Iam videamus, quae contra nostra excogitaris,
units.tr: But even if we were to grant most readily that God wished those who eat leaven to be driven from the feast of unleavened bread, it would nonetheless be false that he therefore commanded those who live more licentiously and wickedly to be driven away from our sacraments. For the feast of unleavened bread, as has already been said, signifies not the Lord's Supper but the whole time of our pilgrimage. Therefore the wicked man is to be excluded not from the Lord's Supper but from life. It is a long way from being killed or cut off to being removed from the sacraments or excommunicated. Now if we were also to grant that the cutting off which God threatens to those who eat leaven signified removal from the sacraments, it would still be false, namely that those who eat leavened bread thereby figured wicked men as you wish. For Moses could not be defended from a manifest contradiction. For these two statements are contradictory: "Everyone who is clean according to the law shall eat the Passover under penalty of being cut off," and "some who are clean according to the law, that is, who have committed some sin, shall not eat the Passover." From these things it is sufficiently clear how weak and slippery are the things you draw from this ceremony in defence of your excommunication. Now let us see what you have devised against our position.

units.la: CAP. VII. Defensio sententiae nostrae de Fermento.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII. A Defence of our opinion concerning Leaven.

units.la: Absurdum esse dixi, imò impossibile, nullo que pacto credendum, Deum eodem tempore apertis verbis mandare aliquid, & idem eodem tempore eisdémque hominibus tacè & sub figura vetare. Praecipit aperte, mandatumque aliquoties repetit, ut omnes circumcisi, exceptis solis legaliter immundis & abstentibus, ter singulis annis coram Deo compareant cum aliquo munere, & festa simul concelebrent. Quis ergo audeat dicere, Deum eodem tempore sub velamine fermenti idem hoc voluisse prohibere? Certè contradictoria simul iuberet, quod impium est cogitare. Ad haec quid tu? Concedimus, inquis, totum argumentum: nec alios praeter immundos arcemus. Haec tu. An non aduertis, quàm candidè agas? Argumentum nostrum loquitur de immunditia legis: tu respondes de impuritate morum.
